data.title: Cloud Run GPUs, now GA, makes running AI workloads easier for everyone
data.author: mariuz
data.article_summary: Google Cloud宣布其无服务器服务Cloud Run正式支持NVIDIA GPU，使其适用于各种AI工作负载。关键优势包括按秒计费、自动缩放至零以节省成本、快速启动（5秒内启动GPU实例）、以及对HTTP和WebSocket流媒体的全面支持。该功能现已全球可用，无需申请配额，任何人都可使用NVIDIA L4 GPU。Cloud Run还提供多区域部署选项，目前支持五个区域，并计划增加更多。此外，GPU支持也扩展至Cloud Run Jobs，适用于批处理和异步任务，如模型微调和批量AI推理。该功能提高了AI计算的可访问性和成本效益。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google Cloud Run及其GPU服务的优缺点、价格对比以及与其他服务的比较

不同观点：
• Ashishb认为Google Cloud Run整体不错，但其GPU服务不具成本效益，实例计费昂贵且模型加载/卸载速度慢，推荐使用VM+GPU的组合。
• Isoprophlex对大云供应商的复杂性和潜在的高昂费用表示担忧，更倾向于使用Modal和vast.ai。
• Mythz提供了详细的定价对比，显示Google的GPU价格相比runpod.io和vast.ai更高，且Google假设全月24/7运行，而其他服务按秒计费。
• Jbarrow是Modal的粉丝，称赞其无服务器且可缩放至零的GPU服务，并期待其他大供应商也提供类似服务。
• Montebicyclelo指出Cloud Run的自动缩放和成本控制优势，但仅使用了CPU版本。
• Huksley提到一个更便宜的欧盟GPU云供应商DataCrunch，其价格比Run Pod等更低。
• Gabe_monroy作为Google Cloud Run和GKE的负责人，欢迎大家提问并参与讨论。
• Albeebe1对Cloud Run的简单和成本效益表示赞赏，基于之前在vertex.ai上的高额费用经历。
• Pier25询问Google Cloud Run的GPU定价与Fly GPUs的比较。
• Jjuliano作为kdeps.com的开发者，分享了使用Google Cloud Run的积极经验。
• Einpoklum质疑为何商业广告会作为内容文章发布。
• Aeolun认为每小时67美分的GPU实例价格不错，但不确定T4 GPU的性能如何。
• Lemming理解为可以运行任意模型且在使用不频繁时非常便宜，认为这非常有价值。
• Holografix指出该服务适合运行小型自定义模型或最新的开放权重模型，但对已有像Llama这样的模型访问服务表示质疑。
• Gardnr解释了Nvidia L4 GPU的规格，认为其适合推理任务。

补充讨论：
• 价格比较是讨论的核心，用户对不同服务商的GPU价格和计费模式进行了详细对比。
• 自动缩放和成本控制是Cloud Run被广泛认可的优点，但也有人指出其实例计费和模型加载速度问题。
• 不同用户对各种无服务器GPU服务的偏好不同，有人更喜欢Modal、vast.ai等新兴服务。
• 有用户对商业广告内容的出现表示不满，表明社区对内容纯净度的关注。

争议焦点：
• Google Cloud Run GPU服务是否具备成本效益和性能优势是讨论的主要争议点。用户对其实例计费和模型加载速度存在质疑，而有人则认为其自动缩放和易用性是优势。

44178468.article_content:
Serverless
Cloud Run GPUs, now GA, makes running AI workloads easier for everyone
June 2, 2025
Steren Giannini
Director, Product Management
Yunong Xiao
Director, Engineering
Try Gemini 2.5
Our most intelligent model is now available on Vertex AI
Try now
Developers love
Cloud Run
, Google Cloud’s serverless runtime,
for its simplicity, flexibility, and scalability. And today, we’re thrilled to announce that NVIDIA GPU support for Cloud Run is now generally available, offering a powerful runtime for a variety of use cases that’s also remarkably cost-efficient.
Now, you can enjoy the following benefits across both GPUs and CPUs:
Pay-per-second billing
: You are only charged for the GPU resources you consume, down to the second.
Scale to zero
: Cloud Run automatically scales your GPU instances down to zero when no requests are received, eliminating idle costs. This is a game-changer for sporadic or unpredictable workloads.
Rapid startup and scaling
Go from zero to an instance with a GPU and drivers installed in under 5 seconds, allowing your applications to respond to demand very quickly. For example, when scaling from zero (cold start), we achieved an impressive Time-to-First-Token of approximately 19 seconds for a gemma3:4b model (this includes startup time, model loading time, and running the inference)
Full streaming support
: Build truly interactive applications with out-of-the box support for HTTP and WebSocket streaming, allowing you to provide LLM responses to your users as they are generated.
Support for GPUs in Cloud Run is a significant milestone, underscoring our leadership in making GPU-accelerated applications simpler, faster, and more cost-effective than ever before.
“Serverless GPU acceleration represents a major advancement in making cutting-edge AI computing more accessible. With seamless access to NVIDIA L4 GPUs, developers can now bring AI applications to production faster and more cost-effectively than ever before.”
- Dave Salvator, director of accelerated computing products, NVIDIA
Try Google Cloud for free
Start building with $300 in free credits for new customers. All customers get free usage of 20+ products, up to monthly limits.
Get started for free
AI inference for everyone
One of the most exciting aspects of this GA release is that Cloud Run GPUs are now available to everyone for NVIDIA L4 GPUs, with
no quota request required
.This removes a significant barrier to entry, allowing you to immediately tap into GPU acceleration for your Cloud Run services. Simply use
--gpu 1
from the Cloud Run command line, or check the "GPU" checkbox in the console, no need to request quota:
Production-ready
With general availability, Cloud Run with GPU support is now covered by Cloud Run's
Service Level Agreement (SLA)
, providing you with assurances for reliability and uptime. By default, Cloud Run offers
zonal redundancy
, helping to ensure enough capacity for your service to be resilient to a zonal outage; this also applies to Cloud Run with GPUs. Alternatively, you can turn off zonal redundancy and benefit from a
lower price
for best-effort failover of your GPU workloads in case of a zonal outage.
Multi-regional GPUs
To support global applications, Cloud Run GPUs are available in five Google Cloud
regions
: us-central1 (Iowa, USA), europe-west1 (Belgium), europe-west4 (Netherlands), asia-southeast1 (Singapore), and asia-south1 (Mumbai, India), with more to come.
Cloud Run also
simplifies deploying your services across multiple regions
. For instance, you can deploy a service across the US, Europe and Asia with a single command, providing global users with lower latency and higher availability. For instance, here’s how to deploy
Ollama
, one of the easiest way to run open models, on Cloud Run across three regions:
Loading...
gcloud run deploy my-global-service \
--image ollama/ollama --port 11434 \
--gpu 1 \
--regions us-central1,europe-west1,asia-southeast1
See it in action: 0 to 100 NVIDIA GPUs in four minutes
You can witness the incredible scalability of Cloud Run with GPUs for yourself with
this live demo
from Google Cloud Next 25, showcasing how we scaled from 0 to 100 GPUs in just four minutes.
Load testing a Stable Diffusion service running on Cloud Run GPUs to 100 GPU instances in four minutes.
Unlock new use cases with NVIDIA GPUs on Cloud Run jobs
The power of Cloud Run with GPUs isn't just for real-time inference using request-driven Cloud Run services. We're also excited to announce the availability of GPUs on
Cloud Run jobs
, unlocking new use cases, particularly for batch processing and asynchronous tasks:
Model fine-tuning
: Easily fine-tune a pre-trained model on specific datasets without having to manage the underlying infrastructure. Spin up a GPU-powered job, process your data, and scale down to zero when it’s complete.
Batch AI inferencing
: Run large-scale batch inference tasks efficiently. Whether you're analyzing images, processing natural language, or generating recommendatio

Table of contents
All Collections
Max Plan
Using Claude Code with your Pro or Max Plan
Using Claude Code with your Pro or Max Plan
Updated today
Table of contents
Pro and Max plan subscribers have access to use Claude Code directly in the terminal.
What is Claude Code?
Claude Code is a command line tool that gives you access to Claude models directly in your terminal, allowing you to delegate complex coding tasks while maintaining transparency and control. With Pro and Max plans, you now have access to both Claude in the web, desktop, and mobile apps and Claude Code in your terminal with one unified subscription.
Why use Claude and Claude Code?
Use two powerful AI products in one simple subscription.
Use Claude for writing, research, analysis, and more — at work and at home
Use Claude Code for your terminal-based coding workflows
How to connect Claude Code with your plan
To start using Claude Code with your Pro or Max plan:
Ensure you have an active Pro or Max plan subscription
If you're not already subscribed, upgrade at claude.ai/upgrade
Pro plan: $20/month for light coding work on small repositories
Max plan offers two usage tiers:
5x Pro usage ($100/month)
20x Pro usage ($200/month)
Install Claude Code
Visit the
Claude Code documentation page
to download and install Claude Code
Follow the installation instructions for your operating system
Authenticate with your Claude credentials
When prompted during setup or first use, log in with the same credentials you use for Claude
This will connect your Pro or Max plan subscription to Claude Code
If you're already logged in to Claude Code via Anthropic Console PAYG, run /login from within Claude Code to switch to your subscription plan
How Rate Limits Work
Both Pro and Max plans offer rate limits that are shared across Claude and Claude Code, meaning all activity in both tools counts against the same usage limits. The number of messages you can send varies based on message length, conversation length, and file attachments, while Claude Code usage varies based on project complexity, codebase size, and auto-accept settings.
Pro Plan
To read more about Pro plan usage limits, see
About Claude Pro usage
.
Pro ($20/month)
: Average users can send approximately 45 messages with Claude every 5 hours, OR send approximately 10-40 prompts with Claude Code every 5 hours
Model access
: Pro plan subscribers can access Sonnet 4, but won’t be able to use Opus 4 with Claude Code
Best for
: Light work on small repositories (typically under 1,000 lines of code)
Max Plan
For detailed information about Max plan usage limits, see
About Claude's Max Plan Usage
.
Max 5x Pro ($100/month)
: Average users can send approximately 225 messages with Claude every 5 hours, OR send approximately 50-200 prompts with Claude Code every 5 hours
Max 20x Pro ($200/month)
: Average users can send approximately 900 messages with Claude every 5 hours, OR send approximately 200-800 prompts with Claude Code every 5 hours
Model access
: Max plan subscribers can use Sonnet or Opus 4 on Claude Code (switch between them using the
/model
command)
Best for
: Everyday use with larger codebases, or power users
These estimates are based on how Claude works today. In the future, we'll add new capabilities (some might use more of your usage, others less) but we're always working to give you the best value on your current plan.
What Happens When You Hit Rate Limits
To help you monitor your usage, you will see warning messages about remaining capacity. When you reach your rate limits, you can select from a few options based on your needs:
Pro Plan Users
Consider upgrading to the Max plan (5x Pro/$100) if you consistently hit limits and need more capacity for larger repositories
You will have the flexibility to switch to
pay-as-you-go usage
with an Anthropic Console account for intensive coding sprints
Wait until your rate limits reset
Max Plan Users
If you're on the $100 Max plan (5x Pro usage), consider upgrading to the $200 Max plan (20x Pro usage) if you consistently hit limits
You will have the flexibility to switch to
pay-as-you-go usage
with an Anthropic Console account for intensive coding sprints
Wait until your rate limits reset
For more details on efficient usage, refer to our
Usage Limit Best Practices
.
Claude Code Usage Limits and Billing
Understanding Two Distinct Systems
It's important to recognize these are separate systems:
Claude Code
: Presents options for continuing usage through API credits
API Console
: Contains optional auto-reload settings for API credit management where your terminal is located
Choosing to Use API Credits
If you want to use API credits through Claude Code:
Usage will be billed at standard API rates (distinct from Pro/Max Plan pricing)
If auto-reload is enabled in your Console account, additional credits will be automatically added when your balance runs low
Staying Within Your Plan
To maintain usage strictly within your Pro or Max Plan allocation:
Decline the API credit option

data.title: Distance-Based ISA for Efficient Register Management
data.author: abhi9u
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了随着CPU核心并行处理能力的提升，特别是在宽度上的显著增加，传统的寄存器管理方法面临的挑战。尽管RISC-V等新型指令集架构（ISA）在设计上进行了优化，但寄存器重命名过程的复杂性和成本仍是瓶颈。文章提出了一种基于距离的ISA设计，通过指定操作数产生时间而非寄存器编号（如add ^2 ^3），避免了伪依赖问题。这种方法类似于编译器中的静态单赋值（SSA）形式，能有效减少寄存器重命名的复杂性，并提升CPU的并行处理效率。这种创新的ISA设计为解决未来处理器中指令调度和寄存器管理问题提供了新思路。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：评论者们对某篇论文或研究中的CPU架构及其新颖性、实现方式和性能表现进行了讨论。

不同观点：
• [thechao] 对论文作者的前期研究工作表示怀疑，认为他们在开展工作前可能没有对先验研究进行充分调查。他提到了低层次AI中的可疑重做现象，并将该研究中的CPU架构与90年代IBM发布的Power架构以及Mill CPU进行比较，不确定新架构是否真的具有创新性。
• [ahartmetz] 支持[thechao]的观点，特别指出论文中提到的“基于距离的表示方法”与Mill CPU的“belt”概念相似，暗示新颖性可能不足。
• [stefanha] 关注论文中提到但未详细提供的SPEC CPU性能结果，希望了解更多关于该架构的性能和可扩展性数据。

补充讨论：
• [hyperhello] 提出了一个技术性问题，询问“距离”是指从PC（程序计数器）的绝对地址还是指已执行指令的数量，这显示了对该架构具体实现细节的关注和疑问。
• [thechao] 进一步补充了自己对x64架构中相对地址模式的记忆模糊，认为作者的目标可能是从零开始探索一种全新的实现方式，或者该微架构确实非常独特。

争议焦点：评论者们对该研究中的CPU架构是否真正具有新颖性存在争议，特别是与Mill CPU和IBM的Power架构的比较。此外，对论文未提供详细性能结果表示不满。

44179494.article_content:
Distance-Based ISA for Efficient Register Management
by
Toru Koizumi, Ryota Shioya, Hidetsugu Irie on Apr 2, 2025
| Tags:
Architecture
,
CPU
,
gpu
,
ISA Design
CPU cores have become significantly wider over the past decade. Ten years ago, the highest-performance CPUs could decode only up to four instructions simultaneously and execute up to eight instructions. However, top-tier CPUs released in recent years have grown to nearly twice this width. For example,
Apple’s M4 processor
, released in 2024, can decode 10 instructions simultaneously and execute up to 19 instructions.
ARM’s Cortex-X925 processor
, also released in 2024, can decode 10 instructions simultaneously and execute up to 23 instructions. Furthermore, these processors can dynamically schedule around 700 to 900 instructions out of order. Given the rapid increase in scheduling capacity, it is likely that processors capable of managing over 1000 instructions out-of-order will emerge in the near future.
Figure 1: Comparison of widest CPUs in 2015 and 2025.
To create a CPU core that can execute a large number of instructions in parallel, it is necessary to improve both the architecture—which includes the overall CPU design and the instruction set architecture (ISA) design—and the microarchitecture, which refers to the hardware design that optimizes instruction execution.
Historically, CPU evolution has primarily been driven by microarchitecture innovations, since discarding backward compatibility and changing the fundamental structure of an instruction set is commercially unfeasible. From an academic perspective, extensive research has focused on reducing complexity by organizing scheduling windows hierarchically or clustering them—typical microarchitectural approaches for building wider CPUs [
WIB
,
LTP
]. Researchers have also explored hybrid designs that integrate in-order principles into out-of-order pipelines [
FXA
,
Ballerino
].
However, microarchitecture innovations alone have their limits. To enable CPUs to execute more instructions in parallel (i.e., to extract more instruction-level parallelism), it is also important to revisit the ISA.
One of the most notable recent developments in instruction sets is
RISC-V
. RISC-V is an open instruction set that has attracted attention from both academia and industry, built upon decades of RISC research. RISC-V is often considered a definitive RISC instruction set, as it was carefully designed to avoid past pitfalls, such as reliance on specific hardware characteristics (e.g., delay slots), which have limited the scalability of previous architectures. As a result, many people may think that research into instruction sets for general-purpose CPUs has come to an end, thanks to RISC-V.
Challenges in Register Management
As refined as RISC-V is, it still inherits certain fundamental challenges common to RISC architectures. In particular, the complexity of register management remains a major bottleneck in RISC architectures, including RISC-V, and we will discuss this issue in more detail later. This problem is becoming increasingly serious, especially as CPU designs continue to scale up, a trend mentioned earlier.
Both CPUs introduced at the beginning of this article can execute a certain maximum number of instructions simultaneously, yet they can only decode roughly half as many instructions per cycle. This limitation stems from the register renaming process that follows decoding. Register renaming maps logical registers to physical ones to eliminate false dependencies caused by logical register reuse.
Register renaming requires highly multi-ported memory, which incurs significant chip area and power costs, making it challenging to simply scale up the rename width. Furthermore, managing the mapping table between logical and physical registers is inherently complex and challenging. For instance, when a branch misprediction occurs, all renames associated with the mispredicted instructions must be undone, requiring the mapping table to be restored to its previous state. As the reorder buffer (ROB) size increases, the associated cost scales accordingly.
Distance-Based Instruction Set
Our solution to these issues is a distance-based instruction set. In a typical instruction set, operands are specified by register numbers, as in R1 <- R2 + R3. By contrast, in a distance-based instruction set, each operand is specified based on how many times ago a result was produced. For example, an instruction that adds the results produced two and three instructions earlier could be written as add ^2 ^3.
With this approach, values produced by instructions are never overwritten, eliminating false dependencies. This is conceptually similar to the static single assignment (SSA) form, an intermediate representation (IR) widely used in compilers, where each variable is assigned exactly once. However, while SSA is effective as a compiler IR, directly applying this approach to an instruction set is insufficient to fully represent a p

data.article_summary: 文章介绍了如何在Node.js中实现原生的热模块替换（HMR）。传统的--watch模式在文件变化时会丢弃所有状态，而理想的方式是在模块变化时仅部分更新模块树。文章提出的方案通过使用Node.js内置的`node:module`模块添加钩子，实现无需重启整个进程的HMR功能。核心方法包括使用`FileTree`类将文件树加载到内存，并通过监听文件变化事件来更新模块版本。依赖树的处理确保了当深层依赖变化时，父模块也会更新。文章还展示了如何在模块失效时进行资源清理，例如语法高亮器的重新初始化。这种方法避免了逻辑重复和系统分离的问题，提供了更高效的开发体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Vitest 项目中关于实时重载机制的技术选择，特别是对 Node.js 中 ECMAScript 模块的垃圾回收问题的讨论。

不同观点：
• 一种观点认为，Vitest 项目曾考虑使用 `node:module` 钩子实现实时重载，但最终拒绝了这一方案。原因是，根据 ECMAScript 模块规范，模块通过模块 ID 字符串始终是可访问的，这导致模块无法被垃圾回收。
• 另一种观点是，基于 `node:vm` 的伪模块则可以正常进行垃圾回收，当它们变得不可访问时，能够被系统回收资源。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中提到，ECMAScript 模块在浏览器环境中被认为是可接受的，因为浏览器标签页通常会被关闭或重新加载，但在长时间运行的服务器进程中，这种无法垃圾回收的特性被认为是不合适的。
• 争议的焦点在于 ECMAScript 模块的内存管理问题，特别是在服务器环境中的长期运行进程对内存消耗的敏感性，相比之下，伪模块方案可能更适合这种场景。

总结：讨论围绕 Vitest 项目在实现实时重载时对模块系统的选择，重点分析了 ECMAScript 模块的垃圾回收问题及其在不同运行环境中的适用性。

#
HMR natively in Node.js (technical write up)
One of the key factors in rapid development is
discarding as little state as possible.
In Node.js, this means the new
--watch
flags
are not that useful, since they throw everything away.
The ideal is to simply invalidate a module when it changes
or when a module it depends on changes.
This way, all imports and data are always fresh,
but only partial module trees get re-evaluated.
Previously, immaculata did the same thing Vite does now:
use the built-in
node:vm
functionality to create
an ad hoc module system that sits on top of Node's,
and glues these systems together using custom logic.
This effectively creates second class modules.
The main drawbacks are that logic is duplicated and separated.
Duplication happens in finding and loading files, parsing them,
evaluating and storing their module objects, and gluing all these
together with each other and with Node's own module system.
And these systems are inherently separate, so that
native Node module hooks will have no effect on the ad hoc system.
By adding module hooks using Node's built-in
node:module
module,
it's now possible to implement "hot module" functionality natively.
First, we load source files from disk and keep them in memory.
This won't hit memory limits for most projects and dev machines.
To handle this need, we have a
FileTree
class,
which does nothing other than load a file tree into memory,
and optionally keep it up to date via
.watch()
,
which returns an
EventEmitter
with a
filesUpdated
event.
Node's native file watcher is now disk efficient,
and returns all the information we need,
so we don't need
chokidar
for this.
Next, we have the
useTree
dual-hook which does two key things.
First, it implements a loader hook that returns the source
string
using
tree.files.get
instead of
fs.readFileSync
.
Second, it implements a resolver hook that appends
?ver=${file.version}
to the URL of any given module.
What ties all of this together is the fact that
the
FileTree
constructor and the
watch
method
both set each file's
version
to
Date.now()
.
This becomes an automatic query busting string,
which works because Node internally uses URLs
to represent all modules.
In practice, this means that we can import a module file initially,
and import the same file again after the
filesUpdated
event,
and either the cached module object will be returned,
or the file will be re-evaluated if it was updated.
The one missing piece of this puzzle was dependency trees.
Because module hooks are called during import,
we can use this information to register dependencies,
which is done internally within
FileTree
.
Each time a dependency of a module changes,
the parent module itself also has its version updated.
This works recursively, so that modules are always fresh,
and updated even if a single deep dependency changes.
The code to use these hooks is relatively short and simple.
import
{
FileTree
}
from
"immaculata"
import
{
useTree
}
from
"immaculata/hooks.js"
import
{
registerHooks
}
from
'node:module'
const
tree
=
new
FileTree
(
'src'
,
import
.
meta
.
dirname
)
registerHooks
(
useTree
(
tree
))
const
myModule
=
await
import
(
'src/myModule.js'
)
// src/myModule.js is executed
const
myModule2
=
await
import
(
'src/myModule.js'
)
// src/myModule.js is NOT executed a second time
tree
.
watch
().
on
(
'filesUpdated'
,
async
()
=>
{
const
myModule
=
await
import
(
'src/myModule.js'
)
// src/myModule.js IS executed again iff invalidated
})
As a consequence of having a dependency tree,
we can easily send a
moduleInvalidated
event
at the same time that we update its
version
.
And because trees are just objects,
we can import them from a module that
needs to cleanup resources on invalidation.
This site uses Shiki for syntax highlighting,
which requires that you use it as a singleton.
Calling its
dispose
method on invalidation
allows me to edit the syntax highlighting file
without having to restart the whole process.
(This code is taken verbatim from this site.)
import
*
as
ShikiMd
from
'@shikijs/markdown-it'
import
type
MarkdownIt
from
'markdown-it'
import
*
as
Shiki
from
'shiki'
import
{
tree
}
from
'../../static.ts'
const
highlighter
=
await
Shiki
.
createHighlighter
({
themes:
[
'dark-plus'
],
langs:
[
'tsx'
,
'typescript'
,
'json'
,
'yaml'
,
'bash'
],
})
export
function
highlightCode
(
md
:
MarkdownIt
) {
md
.
use
(
ShikiMd
.
fromHighlighter
(
highlighter
, {
theme:
'dark-plus'
}))
}
tree
.
onModuleInvalidated
(
import
.
meta
.
url
, ()
=>
{
highlighter
.
dispose
()
})

data.title: What if you could do it all over? (2020)
data.author: FinnLobsien
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了作者在1990年代末期作为大学生和技术创始人的经历。他与两位室友合并了各自的高中网络公司，成立了一家“青少年巨头公司”，为不同客户制作网站和软件。在1999年，他们接手了一个类似Slack的项目，尽管面临挑战，他们成功完成了任务并过上了一段奢华的生活。然而，随着互联网泡沫破裂，他们的客户被收购，项目无疾而终，公司也随之关闭。在毕业后，作者选择了与女友（后来的妻子）一起攻读英语研究生，最终成为记者，过上了与之前创业生活截然不同的生活。文章最后引用了Andrew H. Miller的书中观点，探讨了未选择的人生道路和个人身份的思考，强调了人生选择的单一性和其带来的可能性缩减，尽管未实现的潜力令人遗憾，但也赋予了现有生活特殊的意义。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对“未经历的生活”的思考及其对当前生活的影响

不同观点：
• **专注于感恩与满足**：jmathai认为，专注于感恩可以帮助他珍惜当下，而不是沉湎于未曾经历的生活。这种观点强调了对现有生活的满足感。
• **不断迎接新生活的可能性**：futureshock认为生活充满了新的可能性，如新的职业、城市、国家、朋友和家庭。他强调了对新生活机会的开放态度，并认为随着时间的推移，能够更好地识别值得投入的新生活。
• **生命如梦，享受当下**：runamuck分享了他的一种超然态度，认为生命如梦，世界如过眼云烟。他主张享受生活并传播爱。
• **生命重演的思考实验**：matwood提到了一本名为《Replay》的书，这本书探讨了生命重演的问题，并认为这种思考能够帮助人们看清生活中真正重要的东西。
• **对未来生活的乐观期待**：glimshe对自己当前的生活感到满意，但更感兴趣的是未来生活，尤其是未来科技和生活的可能性。他表达了对未来生活的乐观期待。
• **对未选择道路的积极想象**：999900000999分享了他对未选择道路的积极想象，尤其是那些成功的可能性。他强调了对当前生活的满足，并认为这些想象大多是正面的。
• **对未来知识的假设**：rwmj认为，如果拥有完美的未来知识，人们会选择投资于成功的企业，而不是从头开始创建。这种观点质疑了对未来重来的实际价值。
• **对过去生活的无奈接受**：os2warpman提到，他常常思考已故朋友和战友的未经历生活，认为过去的不可改变。他强调了对当前生活的接受，并认为对过去生活的假设是徒劳的。
• **对时间旅行的拒绝**：javier_e06和mgh95都表达了对时间旅行的拒绝态度，认为一次生命的体验已经足够。
• **对当前决定的坚持**：lnsru强调了他对过去决定的坚持，认为即使这些决定不完美，他也不愿意重来一次。他期待未来的可能性，并对当前生活感到兴奋。
• **对过去与未来改变的思考**：jebarker质疑了关于未经历生活的讨论，认为过去和未来的改变是两种不同的概念。他表达了对未来改变的渴望，而不是对过去生活的假设。
• **对孩子存在的珍视**：theletterf认为，他不会选择改变自己的生活，因为不愿意在任何可能的平行宇宙中失去自己的孩子。
• **对居住选择的反思**：anonzzzies希望能够更早地搬离城市，表达了对过去居住选择的反思。

补充讨论：
• **对未经历生活的不同态度**：一些人如jmathai和glimshe认为应该专注于当前的生活并感恩，而另一些人如futureshock和999900000999则对未经历的生活充满好奇和期待。
• **对时间旅行的不同看法**：javier_e06和mgh95拒绝时间旅行的想法，而rwmj和futureshock则探讨了时间旅行和重新选择的假设价值。
• **对过去生活的接受与无奈**：os2warpman和lnsru都强调了对过去生活的无奈接受，并认为当前的生活是最好的选择。
• **对未来生活的期待与乐观**：glimshe、futureshock和lnsru都表达了对未来生活的期待和乐观态度，认为未来的可能性更加值得探索。

争议焦点：
• **未经历生活的假设价值**：对未经历生活的假设是否具有实际意义和价值，存在不同看法。一些人认为这些假设是徒劳的，而另一些人则认为这些假设能够帮助人们看清生活中真正重要的东西。
• **对过去和未来改变的态度**：对过去生活的假设与对未来改变的渴望之间存在不同的观点和态度，一些人更关注过去的生活，而另一些人则更期待未来的可能性。

Once, in another life, I was a tech founder. It was the late nineties, when the Web was young, and everyone was trying to cash in on the dot-com boom. In college, two of my dorm mates and I discovered that we’d each started an Internet company in high school, and we merged them to form a single, teen-age megacorp. For around six hundred dollars a month, we rented office space in the basement of a building in town. We made Web sites and software for an early dating service, an insurance-claims-processing firm, and an online store where customers could “bargain” with a cartoon avatar for overstock goods. I lived large, spending the money I made on tuition, food, and a stereo.
In 1999—our sophomore year—we hit it big. A company that wired mid-tier office buildings with high-speed Internet hired us to build a collaborative work environment for its customers: Slack, avant la lettre. It was a huge project, entrusted to a few college students through some combination of recklessness and charity. We were terrified that we’d taken on work we couldn’t handle but also felt that we were on track to create something innovative. We blew through deadlines and budgets until the C-suite demanded a demo, which we built. Newly confident, we hired our friends, and used our corporate AmEx to expense a “business dinner” at Nobu. Unlike other kids, who were what—socializing?—I had a business card that said “Creative Director.” After midnight, in our darkened office, I nestled my Aeron chair into my
IKEA
desk, queued up Nine Inch Nails in Winamp, scrolled code, peeped pixels, and entered the matrix. After my client work was done, I’d write short stories for my creative-writing workshops. Often, I slept on the office futon, waking to plunder the vending machine next to the loading dock, where a homeless man lived with his cart.
I liked this entrepreneurial existence—its ambition, its scrappy, near-future velocity. I thought I might move to San Francisco and work in
tech
. I saw a path, an opening into life. But, as the dot-com bubble burst, our client’s business was acquired by a firm that was acquired by another firm that didn’t want what we’d made. Our invoices went unpaid. It was senior year—a fork in the road. We closed our business and moved out of the office. A few days before graduation, when I went to pay my tuition bill, a girl on the elevator struck up a conversation, then got off at her floor; on my ride down, she stepped on for a second time, and our conversation continued. We started dating, then went to graduate school in English together. We got married, I became a journalist, and we had a son. I now have a life, a world, a story. I’m me, not him—whoever he might have turned out to be.
“The thought that I might have become someone else is so bland that dwelling on it sometimes seems fatuous,” the literary scholar Andrew H. Miller writes, in “
On Not Being Someone Else: Tales of Our Unled Lives
” (Harvard). Still, phrased the right way, the thought has an insistent, uncanny magnetism. Miller’s book is, among other things, a compendium of expressions of wonder over what might have been. Miller quotes Clifford Geertz, who, in “
The Interpretation of Cultures
,” wrote that “one of the most significant facts about us may finally be that we all begin with the natural equipment to live a thousand kinds of life but end in the end having lived only one.” He cites the critic William Empson: “There is more in the child than any man has been able to keep.” We have unlived lives for all sorts of reasons: because we make choices; because society constrains us; because events force our hand; most of all, because we are singular individuals, becoming more so with time. “While growth realizes, it narrows,” Miller writes. “Plural possibilities simmer down.” This is painful, but it’s an odd kind of pain—hypothetical, paradoxical. Even as we regret who we haven’t become, we value who we are. We seem to find meaning in what’s never happened. Our self-portraits use a lot of negative space.
For some people, imagining unlived lives is torture, even a gateway to crisis. Miller tells the story of Spencer Brydon, the protagonist of Henry James’s tale “
The Jolly Corner
.” As a young man, Brydon left America for Europe, where he “followed strange paths and worshiped strange gods,” living as a playboy. Three decades later, he returns to New York, where he takes stock of his peers. Many of them are rich, powerful, or respected; they have built substantial lives. Brydon, who is single and only superficially accomplished, starts to wonder how he would have turned out if he’d stayed. Would he have become a successful businessman? Married his friend Alice, with whom he’s reconnected? He begins to spend his nights prowling the hallways of his childhood home, convinced that the ghost of the man he might have been wanders there. • **对当前决定的坚持**：lnsru强调了他对过去决定的坚持，认为即使这些决定不完美，他也不愿意重来一次。他期待未来的可能性，并对当前生活感到兴奋。

data.title: Tellico – Collection management software
data.author: Tomte
data.article_summary: Tellico是一款能够自动从互联网获取数据的工具，支持多种数据源，节省手动输入时间。它提供预定义的收藏类别，如书籍、视频游戏和硬币，并允许用户自定义信息字段或创建自己的收藏类别。此外，Tellico利用Qt和KDE框架实现桌面集成、功能扩展和界面一致性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：软件工具的适用性及现代需求

不同观点：
• [slightwinder] 认为 Tellico 是一款很棒的应用，曾在十年前使用过，但后来由于不再符合其使用需求而放弃。他认为在当前经济环境下，Tellico 显得有些过时，人们更可能使用像 Obsidian 或 Notion 这样的现代工具。不过，他对 Tellico 依然存在并不断发展表示认可。

• [sundarurfriend] 提到 Data Crow 在他开始认真研究时停止了维护，导致他放弃了使用目录软件的想法。他对发现一个积极维护且功能丰富的替代品（Tellico）表示赞赏，并认为其基于 KDE 是一个不错的加分项。

• [layer8] 认为 Tellico 虽然看起来不错，但在当今没有移动支持的情况下，很难成为一个可行的选择。

补充讨论：
• slightwinder 对现代工具如 Obsidian 和 Notion 的提及，反映了对软件工具在现代经济和工作环境下的不同需求。
• sundarurfriend 的评论强调了软件维护和持续支持对用户选择的重要性。
• layer8 指出了移动支持在现代应用中的关键性，提出了对 Tellico 功能缺失的担忧。

争议焦点：Tellico 在现代应用环境中的适用性，尤其是在移动支持方面的不足，是主要争议点。这影响了不同用户对其作为长期解决方案的可行性看法。

data.title: Click-V: A RISC-V emulator built with ClickHouse SQL
data.author: calcifer
data.article_summary:
这篇文章介绍了一个使用ClickHouse SQL构建的RISC-V模拟器（Click-V），使ClickHouse接近图灵完备。该项目目前主要作为备份，尚未完全对开发者友好。模拟器通过插入命令触发一系列物化视图和空表来模拟读写寄存器和内存。它使用Redis处理寄存器和内存，但由于ClickHouse的KVStorage逻辑存在问题，性能受限，当前CPU运行速度约为17Hz。

要运行该模拟器，需设置ClickHouse和Redis服务器，执行SQL文件中的语句，并通过特定插入命令加载RISC-V程序。可以通过一系列SQL查询监控程序状态，如显示指令、寄存器、内存和控制台等。此外，系统还支持通过ClickOS UDF实现系统调用，处理文件和网络访问。文章还提到一个Rust演示程序，展示了如何在模拟器中运行。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于在ClickHouse上构建音乐合成器的评论和不同观点

不同观点：
• [zX41ZdbW] 分享了一个基于ClickHouse的音乐合成器项目链接，展示了ClickHouse的一种创新应用，强调其技术可行性与创造性。

• [hobs] 对此表示惊讶，并带有一定的调侃，认为这是"精神伤害"级别的创意，暗示这种将SQL用于音乐合成的想法超出了常规认知。同时提到自己曾见过一些可怕的SQL应用，但这个ClickOS UDF（用户定义函数）更让人震惊。这表明对该项目感到意外，甚至有些不安，但同时也承认其独特性。

• [blyry] 表达了对此项目的兴奋，并提到自己曾考虑过类似的想法，但计划基于PostgreSQL实现。他提出了一个技术性问题，询问为什么选择ClickHouse而不是PostgreSQL，并分享了自己的思路：将每个操作视为插入操作，并通过事务记录CPU状态。这表明他对项目的技术选型有疑问，并且对实现细节有浓厚兴趣。

补充讨论：
• [hobs] 的评论带有些许幽默感，表达了对这种创新应用的惊讶，可能隐含了对SQL超出常规用途的某种抵触或不适应。

• [blyry] 对项目的实现方式表现出强烈兴趣，并提出了自己的技术设想，显示出对不同数据库系统在类似项目中的适用性的探讨。

• 争议焦点：选择ClickHouse而非PostgreSQL的原因成为讨论中的一个疑问点，[blyry] 明确提出了这个问题，表明在技术社区中，不同数据库系统的选择常常是一个值得讨论的话题。

• 值得注意的是，尽管存在不同观点，所有评论者都对该项目的创新性表示了认可和兴趣。

Click-V
A RISC-V emulator built with ClickHouse SQL.
This emulator makes ClickHouse truly Turing complete. We are one step closer to running ClickHouse in ClickHouse.
This project/repository isn't dev-friendly yet, I'm just uploading it here as a backup in case my PC catches fire.
How it works
The system will react to the following insert command:
INSERT INTO
clickv
.
clock
(_)
VALUES
()
This command will trigger a large set of branched materialized views and
Null
tables that filter out the program's instructions to simulate reading/writing from registers and memory.
External host machine access works via a single UDF with a custom binary format that gets read/written as an
Array(UInt8)
.
The program is able to perform any logic. Printing to a console table and drawing are built-in.
It can also open/close/read/write/seek files and sockets via the ClickOS UDF.
For more details, see the
architecture
section.
Performance
I tried to use every optimization trick in the book to get this to run fast, unfortunately there is a MAJOR bottleneck to the performance of this emulator due to a bug in ClickHouse KVStorage logic. Because ClickHouse doesn't have an internal KV-type storage engine, I use Redis for registers/memory. But there is a bug with
allow_experimental_analyzer=1
where instead of doing a single
MGET
, it will
SCAN
all keys and
then
MGET
multiple times.
I haven't submitted a bug report yet, but I did investigate it. More notes are commented in the file
/sql/click-v.sql:11
.
As it is now, the CPU runs at around
17hz
, but during early development this was significantly higher. It
can
perform better, but when every almost every instruction depends on a register read, it kills performance quickly. It gets worse with more memory allocated in the emulator.
How to run
Steps:
Set up a ClickHouse v24 image
Set up a Redis-like server for registers/memory access (plain redis works fine, dragonfly was slower, there's also a built-in server in
/system/mem
)
Run all SQL statements in
/sql/click-v.sql
(confirm your redis host is correct, right now it points to
host.docker.internal:6379
)
Load your own RISC-V 32i program into
INSERT INTO clickv.load_program (hex) VALUES ('FFFFFFFF')
(make sure your hex instructions are in the correct direction)
Either clock the system via
INSERT INTO clickv.clock (_) VALUES ()
, or use the auto-clock in
/system/clock
You can now monitor the program with the following commands:
Show program instructions + current instruction:
SELECT * FROM clickv.display_program;
Show all 32 registers:
SELECT * FROM clickv.display_registers;
Show memory (with o parameter for offset):
SELECT * FROM clickv.display_memory(o=1024);
Show console:
SELECT * FROM clickv.display_console FORMAT TSV;
Setup live view (optional):
SET allow_experimental_live_view = 1;
(After frame setup) Show current drawn frame:
SELECT * FROM clickv.display_frame FORMAT RawBLOB;
(After frame setup) Show live-updating frame:
WATCH clickv.display_frame FORMAT RawBLOB;
For more help/commands, see the bottom of
/sql/click-v.sql
file.
ROM/RAM/Graphics Memory is configurable.
Components
ClickHouse
Depends on ClickHouse v24.
No other setup is required for basic emulator.
For handling syscalls, you will need to set up the ClickOS UDF, but this is optional.
Clock
path:
/system/cmd/clock
This program simply runs the clock for you, as fast as possible.
Will output clock speed and total cycles to console.
ClickOS
path:
/system/cmd/clickos-server
path:
/system/cmd/clickos-client
Optional program to give the emulated program access to the host system/network.
This is a client/server application.
The client runs as a ClickHouse executable UDF, and then forwards requests to the server.
The server will then handle all syscalls (such as reading/writing to a file, opening a UDP socket, etc.)
You will need to set up the UDF in your ClickHouse server. Easiest way is to make two Docker volume binds: one to the UDF XML, and the other to built binary (you must
go build
for your docker env/arch)
Run the server to listen/handle syscalls. File paths are relative to the working directory of the ClickOS server process.
rs-demo
path:
/rs-demo
This is a demo rust program that can be compiled to run in the emulator.
I have some boilerplate for syscalls, with some OS abstractions for
read
,
write
,
seek
,
socket
,
open
,
close
, etc.

data.article_summary: 2023年9月，全球观测到一种奇特的间隔90秒的地震信号，持续九天，一个月后再次出现。近一年后，研究发现这些信号源于格陵兰东部峡湾由冰川融化引发的两次大规模山体滑坡和由此产生的巨型海啸。海啸在峡湾内形成驻波（seiches），导致这些神秘信号。然而，此前没有直接观察到这些驻波。牛津大学研究人员利用2022年底发射的SWOT卫星的新型雷达干涉仪，成功绘制了海啸后的海水高度变化图，显示水位差异达两米，证实了这一理论。该研究展示了新一代卫星技术在观测海洋极端现象方面的潜力。

June 3, 2025

Greenland's mega tsunamis: First direct observation of the trapped waves that shook the world
by

Copernicus Sentinel-2 satellite image of the Dickson Fjord in East Greenland. Credit: Thomas Monahan.
In September 2023, a bizarre global seismic signal was observed which appeared every 90 seconds over nine days—and was then repeated a month later. Almost a year later, two scientific studies proposed that the cause of these seismic anomalies were two mega tsunamis which were triggered in a remote East Greenland fjord by two major landslides which occurred due to warming of an unnamed glacier.
The waves were thought to have become trapped in the fjord system, forming standing waves (or seiches) that undulated back and forth, causing the mystery signals.
However, up to now no observations of these seiches existed to confirm this theory. Even a Danish military vessel which visited the fjord three days into the first seismic event did not observe the wave which was shaking Earth.
In a new study, Oxford researchers used novel analysis techniques to interpret satellite altimetry data. This measures the height of the Earth's surface (including the ocean) by recording how long it takes for a radar pulse to travel from a satellite to the surface and back again. The work is
published
in
Nature Communications
.
Up to now, conventional satellite altimeters were not able to capture evidence of the wave due to long gaps between observations, and the fact that they sample data directly beneath the spacecraft, producing 1D profiles along the sea-surface. This makes them incapable of depicting the differences in water height needed to spot the waves.
This study used data captured by the new
Surface Water Ocean Topography (SWOT) satellite
, launched in December 2022, to map the height of water across 90% of the Earth's surface.
At the heart of SWOT is the cutting-edge Ka-band Radar Interferometer (KaRIn) instrument, which uses two antennas mounted on a 10-meter boom on either side of the satellite. These two antennas work together to triangulate the return signals that bounce back from the radar pulse—enabling them to measure ocean and surface water levels with unprecedented accuracy (up to 2.5 meters resolution) along a swath 30 miles (50 kilometers) wide.
Copernicus Sentinel-2 satellite image of the Dickson Fjord in East Greenland with the observed sea-surface height measurements from the SWOT satellite of the Earth-shaking wave on October 11th overlaid. Credit: Thomas Monahan.
Using KaRIn data, the researchers made elevation maps of the Greenland Fjord at various timepoints following the two tsunamis. These showed clear, cross-channel slopes with height differences of up to two meters. Crucially, the slopes in these maps occurred in opposite directions, showing that water moved backwards and forwards across the channel.
To prove their theory, the researchers linked these observations to small movements of Earth's crust measured thousands of kilometers away. This connection enabled them to reconstruct the characteristics of the wave, even for periods which the satellite did not observe. The researchers also reconstructed weather and tidal conditions to confirm that the observations could not have been caused by winds or tides.
Lead author Thomas Monahan (DPhil student, Department of Engineering Science, University of Oxford) said, "Climate change is giving rise to new, unseen extremes. These extremes are changing the fastest in remote areas, such as the Arctic, where our ability to measure them using physical sensors is limited. This study shows how we can leverage the next generation of satellite earth observation technologies to study these processes."
"SWOT is a game changer for studying oceanic processes in regions such as fjords which previous satellites struggled to see into."
Co-author Professor Thomas Adcock (Department of Engineering Science, University of Oxford) said, "This study is an example of how the next generation of
satellite
data can resolve phenomena that has remained a mystery in the past.
"We will be able to get new insights into ocean extremes such as tsunamis, storm surges, and freak waves. However, to get the most out of these data we will need to innovate and use both machine learning and our knowledge of ocean physics to interpret our new results."

(2025).

data.title: Record/Replay Debugging Tutorial
data.author: sidkshatriya
data.article_summary: 这篇文章（或网页）标题为"sidkshatriya/me"，内容与GitHub上的一个代码库有关。页面提示用户必须登录才能更改通知设置，并显示该代码库有6次被 fork 和163个星标（star）。这表明该项目在GitHub上有一定的关注度和用户互动。文章主体内容较少，主要是关于代码库的基本信息和互动选项。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何通过一个用C编写的小示例程序使用反向调试来记录/重放和调试程序，包括在macOS上的Linux虚拟机中进行记录/重放。

不同观点：
• 观点一：反向调试是一种强大的调试技术，可以通过工具如GDB和RR（Reverse Debugging）实现。支持者认为，反向调试允许开发者向后回溯程序执行，帮助识别和解决难以发现的bug。示例中提到使用GDB和RR工具在Linux环境下调试C程序，能够捕获程序执行状态并在需要时回放。

• 观点二：在macOS上使用Linux虚拟机进行反向调试是一种可行的解决方案。有评论指出，由于某些工具（如RR）可能在macOS上原生支持不完善，通过虚拟机运行Linux可以解决兼容性问题。这种方法虽然需要额外的设置步骤，但对于跨平台开发者来说是值得的。

• 观点三：反向调试存在一些性能和资源占用的问题。部分讨论提到，反向调试工具如RR会记录程序的每次执行状态，导致额外的内存和存储开销。这可能会影响调试大型程序的效率，尤其在内存和存储资源有限的系统上运行时需要注意。

补充讨论：
• 一些开发者建议使用Docker容器替代虚拟机，以简化设置步骤并提高性能。
• 示例程序的复杂性对调试效果的影响也被提及。简单的小程序容易控制和调试，而大型复杂程序可能需要更高级的调试技术和工具支持。
• 讨论中还提到，反向调试在多线程程序中的应用面临更多挑战，特别是在处理并发和同步问题时，可能需要结合其他调试工具和技术。

争议焦点：主要集中在反向调试工具的性能开销与实际调试需求之间的平衡，以及在不同操作系统上使用这些工具的最佳实践。

data.title: Trump-linked asset manager files Truth Social Bitcoin ETF with SEC
data.article_summary: 一家与特朗普相关的资产管理公司通过纽约证券交易所Arca向美国证券交易委员会（SEC）提交了一份与特朗普的社交媒体平台Truth Social相关的比特币ETF申请。该ETF由Yorkville America Digital管理，计划在纽约证券交易所Arca上市，并跟踪比特币价格。如果获批，它将进入一个已有11只类似基金的市场，包括贝莱德的iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF。这一举动引发了对特朗普与加密货币项目关联的利益冲突和盈利质疑，因其家族涉及多个加密项目，如NFT、memecoin和stablecoin等。此外，特朗普媒体公司还计划在其视频流媒体平台Truth+中整合加密代币和钱包功能。SEC必须在2026年1月29日前对该申请做出决定。

Trump-linked asset manager files Truth Social Bitcoin ETF with SEC
A Bitcoin ETF branded with Donald Trump’s social media platform, Truth Social, is seeking a green light from the Securities and Exchange Commission.
3829
Total views
Listen to article
0:00
News
COINTELEGRAPH IN YOUR SOCIAL FEED
US President Donald Trump’s sprawling crypto empire could grow even larger, as filings show plans for a Bitcoin exchange-traded fund (ETF) branded with his social media platform, Truth Social.
Stock exchange NYSE Arca
filed
for the Truth Social Bitcoin ETF with the Securities and Exchange Commission on June 3 on behalf of crypto asset manager Yorkville America Digital, a partner of Truth Social’s owner, Trump Media & Technology Group.
Trump is the majority owner of Trump Media, but moved his shares into a trust controlled by his son, Donald Trump Jr., before he re-entered the White House.
The ETF seeks to list on the NYSE Arca exchange and track the price of Bitcoin (
BTC
). The filing did not disclose a management fee or ticker but listed Foris DAX Trust Company, the custodian of Crypto.com’s assets, as the proposed custodian.
Source:
Eric Balchunas
If approved, the Trump-linked ETF enters a crowded Bitcoin ETF market of 11 similar funds dominated by BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT) with nearly $69 billion in assets under management.
It could also add to Trump’s controversial ties to crypto,
which critics say
are a conflict of interest with his presidential duties and have accused Trump of profiting from the presidency.
Trump and his family have ties to an increasingly growing number of crypto projects, which include multiple non-fungible token (NFT) collections, two memecoins, a stablecoin, a crypto mining company and a crypto platform with an associated token.
The ETF filing comes after Trump Media
signed an agreement
in April with
Yorkville America Digital
and Crypto.com to launch a series of “Made in America” crypto ETFs.
The 19b-4 filing of the Truth Social Bitcoin ETF effectively initiates the
SEC’s review process
, and it must decide whether to accept, reject or delay the application within 45 days. It can delay its decision multiple times, for a maximum review period of 240 days.
Related:
Donald Trump gives conflicting answers over memecoin profits
The SEC must decide on the application by Jan. 29, 2026, at the latest.
Yorkville will also need to file an S-1 registration statement for the ETF, which informs the SEC what the fund plans to offer, how it will operate, how it intends to use any proceeds raised from investors and associated risks.
Trump Media also filed for a “Truth.Fi Bitcoin Plus ETF” in February, which could receive a portion of the $250 million allocated to its fintech platform,
Truth.Fi
.
Trump Media wants to integrate crypto in video streaming site
Trump Media is also looking to integrate a
crypto token and wallet
into its video streaming site, Truth+, the company’s CEO, Devin Nunes, told shareholders on April 29.
“We’re exploring the introduction of a utility token within a Truth digital wallet that can initially be used to pay for Truth+ subscription costs, and later be applied to other products and services in the Truth ecosphere.”
Trump Media first signaled plans for a potential crypto payments venture last November when it
filed a trademark application
with the US Patent and Trademark Office to build a digital asset wallet and allow crypto payments to be processed on Truth.Fi.

Trump’s crypto ventures raise conflict of interest, insider trading questions

data.title: A Fatal Tesla Crash Shows the Limits of Full Self-Driving
data.author: helsinkiandrew
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：特斯拉自动驾驶系统（FSD/Autopilot）相关的交通安全问题以及是否存在双重标准。

不同观点：
• IcePic认为，尽管特斯拉自动驾驶系统涉及死亡事故，但在其上线的12年中，这是第一起直接归因于自动驾驶系统的事故。他提出，应该对比特斯拉驾驶员在手动驾驶与使用自动驾驶系统时的事故率。如果使用自动驾驶系统能显著降低事故率，那么即使系统不完美，仍然是一个净收益。IcePic还指出，人们对自动驾驶系统的监管要求似乎存在双重标准：人类驾驶引发大量事故，但增加了一些驾驶辅助功能后，人们却急于对这些技术进行更严格的监管。

• Helsinkiandrew提供了与事故相关的存档链接，但没有详细阐述自己的观点，更多是提供信息支持讨论。不过，从其提供的链接可以看出，他可能关注的是事故视频及其影响，尽管存档版本中没有包含相关视频。

补充讨论：
• IcePic还提到对特斯拉"召回200万辆汽车"这一表述的不满，认为这是夸大其词。他解释说，许多所谓的“召回”实际上只是通过软件更新解决问题，并不需要车辆实际返回经销商处进行维修。

• IcePic进一步指出，尽管每起死亡事故都是悲剧，但从整体上看，自动驾驶技术似乎略微提高了驾驶安全性。他推测，如果更多车辆使用类似自动保持车距的功能，事故率可能会进一步下降。

争议焦点：
• 争议的核心在于是否应该对特斯拉的自动驾驶系统采取更严格的监管，以及如何公平地评估自动驾驶系统在减少事故方面的实际效果。IcePic认为存在双重标准，而Helsinkiandrew则通过提供相关链接让人们关注具体事故案例。

data.author: samsmithy
data.article_summary: 上周，中国实验室DeepSeek发布了其R1推理AI模型的更新版本，该模型在多个数学和编程基准测试中表现优异。尽管公司未透露训练数据来源，但有研究者猜测部分数据可能来自谷歌的Gemini系列AI。开发者Sam Paech声称找到了DeepSeek最新模型训练自Gemini输出的证据。此前，DeepSeek的V3模型曾被发现自称为ChatGPT，暗示可能使用了ChatGPT的聊天记录进行训练。OpenAI曾发现DeepSeek使用蒸馏技术，从更大型的模型中提取数据。微软在2024年底发现数据通过OpenAI开发者账户外泄，这些账户据信与DeepSeek有关。尽管AI模型误认和趋同现象常见，但DeepSeek涉嫌利用竞争对手模型数据引发了关注。为防止数据蒸馏，AI公司正加强安全措施，如OpenAI要求组织完成ID验证才能访问某些高级模型。

主要讨论点：OpenAI的条款服务、数据使用及AI模型竞争

不同观点：
• [philipwhiuk] 认为OpenAI禁止用户使用其模型输出用于构建竞争性AI的条款存在双重标准，暗示OpenAI自身在使用他人数据时并没有同样严格的限制。他对此表示不满，带有讽刺意味。
  
• [ksymph] 关注模型输出的语言风格变化，指出Gemini模型在措辞上更加简洁准确，不再像以前那么华丽，认为这与Gemini的行为一致。这里更多是从技术特点和风格变化角度讨论。

• [parineum] 认为当前AI模型之间的数据使用存在相互借鉴的现象，随着生成内容的增加，模型训练数据将变得越来越“近亲繁殖”，最终导致模型性能的趋同和停滞。这里提出了对数据质量和模型发展的长远担忧。

• [vb-8448] 质疑当前谁使用了谁的数据是否还重要，暗示在当前AI发展的阶段，数据使用的界限已经模糊，讨论这个问题可能已经没有实际意义。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是OpenAI的条款是否公平，以及各模型之间数据使用的伦理和合法性问题。
• 对AI模型未来发展的担忧，特别是数据质量下降和模型性能趋同的问题，也被提出作为重要的讨论点。

44179183.article_content:
Last week, Chinese lab DeepSeek released an
updated version of its R1 reasoning AI model
that performs well on a number of math and coding benchmarks. The company didn’t reveal the source of the data it used to train the model, but some AI researchers speculate that at least a portion came from Google’s Gemini family of AI.
Sam Paech, a Melbourne-based developer who creates “emotional intelligence” evaluations for AI, published what he claims is evidence that DeepSeek’s latest model was trained on outputs from Gemini. DeepSeek’s model, called R1-0528, prefers words and expressions similar to those that Google’s Gemini 2.5 Pro favors, said Paech in an
X post
.
If you're wondering why new deepseek r1 sounds a bit different, I think they probably switched from training on synthetic openai to synthetic gemini outputs.
pic.twitter.com/Oex9roapNv
— Sam Paech (@sam_paech)
May 29, 2025
That’s not a smoking gun. But another developer, the pseudonymous creator of a “free speech eval” for AI called
SpeechMap
, noted the DeepSeek model’s traces — the “thoughts” the model generates as it works toward a conclusion — “read like Gemini traces.”
DeepSeek has been accused of training on data from rival AI models before. In December, developers
observed
that DeepSeek’s V3 model often identified itself as ChatGPT, OpenAI’s AI-powered chatbot platform, suggesting that it may’ve been trained on ChatGPT chat logs.
Earlier this year,
OpenAI told the Financial Times
it found evidence linking DeepSeek to the use of distillation, a technique to train AI models by extracting data from bigger, more capable ones.
According to Bloomberg
, Microsoft, a close OpenAI collaborator and investor, detected that large amounts of data were being exfiltrated through OpenAI developer accounts in late 2024 — accounts OpenAI believes are affiliated with DeepSeek.
Distillation isn’t an uncommon practice, but OpenAI’s terms of service prohibit customers from using the company’s model outputs to build competing AI.
To be clear, many models
misidentify
themselves
and converge on the same words and turns of phrases. That’s because the open web, which is where AI companies source the bulk of their training data, is becoming
littered
with AI
slop
. Content farms are using AI to create
clickbait
, and bots are flooding Reddit and
X
.

This “contamination,” if you will, has made it
quite difficult
to thoroughly filter AI outputs from training datasets.
Still, AI experts like Nathan Lambert, a researcher at the nonprofit AI research institute AI2, don’t think it’s out of the question that DeepSeek trained on data from Google’s Gemini.
“If I was DeepSeek, I would definitely create a ton of synthetic data from the best API model out there,” Lambert
wrote
in a post on X. “[DeepSeek is] short on GPUs and flush with cash. It’s literally effectively more compute for them.”
If I was DeepSeek I would definitely create a ton of synthetic data from the best API model out there. Theyre short on GPUs and flush with cash. It’s literally effectively more compute for them. yes on the Gemini distill question.
— Nathan Lambert (@natolambert)
June 3, 2025
Partly in an effort to prevent distillation, AI companies have been ramping up security measures.
In April, OpenAI began
requiring
organizations to complete an ID verification process in order to access certain advanced models. The process requires a government-issued ID from one of the countries supported by OpenAI’s API; China isn’t on the list.
Elsewhere, Google recently began “summarizing” the traces generated by models available through its AI Studio developer platform, a step that makes it more challenging to train performant rival models on Gemini traces. Anthropic in May said it would
start to summarize
its own model’s traces, citing a need to protect its “competitive advantages.”
We’ve reached out to Google for comment and will update this piece if we hear back.

data.title: Quarkdown: A modern Markdown-based typesetting system
data.author: asicsp
data.article_summary: Quarkdown 是一个现代的基于 Markdown 的排版系统，具有强大的扩展功能，能够将项目编译为可打印的书籍或互动演示文稿。它扩展了 CommonMark 和 GFM，支持函数调用、条件语句和循环等编程特性，并提供丰富的标准库，允许用户自定义函数和变量。Quarkdown 支持导出为 HTML、PDF、以及分页文档，兼具快速编译和实时预览功能。相比传统 Markdown、LaTeX 等，Quarkdown 提供更强的文档控制和脚本支持，且易于学习。用户可以通过 Gradle 构建和安装 Quarkdown，并需要 Java 17 或更高版本支持。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：各类Markdown扩展和排版工具的比较与应用

不同观点：
• **KeenWrite的支持者**：用户[thangalin]介绍了KeenWrite的架构和功能，强调了其通过Markdown转换为PDF的能力，以及用于小说写作中变量替换的便利性。他还提供了相关教程和脚本编写指南，展示了如何通过脚本构建Markdown到PDF的转换流程。

• **与Typst的比较**：用户[structural]提出KeenWrite与Typst的比较，并对KeenWrite未提及Typst表示惊讶。这引发了关于这两种工具功能和适用场景的讨论。

• **对Quarkdown的质疑**：用户[blenderob]对Quarkdown的比较表准确性提出质疑，认为LaTeX具有完整的脚本能力，且其功能和学习曲线与Typst相比并无明显优势。

• **与Quarto的比较**：用户[account-5]提到Quarto，指出其与KeenWrite在名称和功能上的相似性，但认为Quarto目前具有更多功能。

• **对模板语言的看法**：用户[looneysquash]不喜欢模板语言中加入函数调用，认为这样会增加切换语言的复杂性，并偏好使用JSX或类似的技术来处理文档生成。

• **对类型排版系统的需求**：用户[rendaw]指出Typst和类似系统主要关注论文排版，而对其他文档类型如表单、传单等的支持不足。

• **对KeenWrite的批评与建议**：用户[krick]希望有一种现代的Markdown based类型排版系统来替代LaTeX，但对KeenWrite的一些设计选择如JVM依赖和语法兼容性提出批评，认为其并未完全满足这一需求。

• **商标问题**：用户[Lammy]提到使用“Quark”一词可能引发的商标问题，并提供了相关链接。

• **与reStructuredText的比较**：用户[cbarrick]认为Quarkdown的语法与reStructuredText类似。

• **对多样化工具的困惑**：用户[AmazingTurtle]对Markdown、Quarkdown、Typst等工具的多样性和不标准化感到困惑，最终选择回归HTML+CSS。

• **对语法设计的建议**：用户[silvestrov]对Quarkdown的函数调用语法提出改进建议，以避免与现有文档关键字冲突。

• **Markdown的纯粹性**：用户[TheEdonian]喜欢Markdown的内容纯粹性，认为其不应包含布局和逻辑，这些可以通过CSS/JS或解释器和主题来实现。

• **LaTeX的成熟性**：用户[bryanhogan]提到在写论文时从Markdown转向LaTeX的经历，虽然LaTeX有其不足，但在学术写作中已非常成熟。

• **PNG输出的需求**：用户[ChuckMcM]提到其使用Pandoc和Template Toolkit生成HTML的需求，并询问是否有工具可以直接输出PNG，以适应其特定的显示需求。

• **现有流程的成熟性**：用户[ryukoposting]使用LaTeX和Markdown混合编写简历，并通过Pandoc转换为PDF，认为现有工具的成熟性使其能够在多年后仍能顺利编译文档。

补充讨论：
- 各类工具如KeenWrite、Typst、Quarto、Quarkdown等的功能对比和适用场景。
- 对模板语言和函数调用的不同看法。
- 对LaTeX的复杂性和成熟性的讨论。
- 对Markdown语法纯粹性和扩展性的不同需求和看法。
- 对输出格式如PDF、PNG等的需求和实现方式。

About
Quarkdown is a modern Markdown-based typesetting system, designed around the key concept of
versatility
, by seamlessly compiling a project
into a print-ready book or an interactive presentation.
All through an incredibly powerful Turing-complete extension of Markdown, ensuring your ideas flow automatically into paper.
Original credits:
Attention Is All You Need
Born as an extension of CommonMark and GFM, the Quarkdown Flavor brings
functions
to Markdown, along with many other syntax extensions.
This is a function call:
.somefunction {arg1} {arg2}
Body argument
Possibilities are unlimited
thanks to an ever-expanding
standard library
,
which offers layout builders, I/O, math, conditional statements and loops.
Not enough?
You can still define your own functions and variables — all within Markdown.
You can even create awesome libraries for everyone to use.
.function {greet}
to from:
**Hello, .to** from .from!
.greet {world} from:{iamgio}
Result:
Hello, world
from iamgio!
This out-of-the-box scripting support opens doors to complex and dynamic content that would be otherwise impossible
to achieve with vanilla Markdown.
Combined with live preview and ⚡ fast compilation speed, Quarkdown simply gets the work done.
Check the
wiki
to learn more about the language and its features.
Check out the demo presentation
here
Built with Quarkdown itself —
source code
(Desktop view is suggested)
As simple as you expect...
Inspired by:
X-ray flashes from a nearby supermassive black hole accelerate mysteriously
...as complex as you need.

✅ Slides
via
reveal.js
✅ Paged (books, articles)
via

Paged documents require a webserver to render in the browser. See the
-p
option below.
PDF
✅ All document types and features supported by HTML are also supported when exporting to PDF.
Check the wiki's
PDF export
page to learn more.
The desired document type can be set by calling the
.doctype
function
within the source itself:
.doctype {slides}
.doctype {paged}

• **商标问题**：用户[Lammy]提到使用“Quark”一词可能引发的商标问题，并提供了相关链接。

• **与reStructuredText的比较**：用户[cbarrick]认为Quarkdown的语法与reStructuredText类似。

• **对多样化工具的困惑**：用户[AmazingTurtle]对Markdown、Quarkdown、Typst等工具的多样性和不标准化感到困惑，最终选择回归HTML+CSS。

• **对语法设计的建议**：用户[silvestrov]对Quarkdown的函数调用语法提出改进建议，以避免与现有文档关键字冲突。

• **Markdown的纯粹性**：用户[TheEdonian]喜欢Markdown的内容纯粹性，认为其不应包含布局和逻辑，这些可以通过CSS/JS或解释器和主题来实现。

• **LaTeX的成熟性**：用户[bryanhogan]提到在写论文时从Markdown转向LaTeX的经历，虽然LaTeX有其不足，但在学术写作中已非常成熟。

• **PNG输出的需求**：用户[ChuckMcM]提到其使用Pandoc和Template Toolkit生成HTML的需求，并询问是否有工具可以直接输出PNG，以适应其特定的显示需求。

• **现有流程的成熟性**：用户[ryukoposting]使用LaTeX和Markdown混合编写简历，并通过Pandoc转换为PDF，认为现有工具的成熟性使其能够在多年后仍能顺利编译文档。

补充讨论：
- 各类工具如KeenWrite、Typst、Quarto、Quarkdown等的功能对比和适用场景。
- 对模板语言和函数调用的不同看法。
- 对LaTeX的复杂性和成熟性的讨论。
- 对Markdown语法纯粹性和扩展性的不同需求和看法。
- 对输出格式如PDF、PNG等的需求和实现方式。

data.title: What do software developers need to know to succeed in an age of AI?
data.author: turadg
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了专业软件开发人员在人工智能时代取得成功所需的知识和技能。通过研究21位处于人工智能应用前沿的开发人员，作者总结了12个工作目标、75个相关任务以及所需的技能和知识，展示了开发人员如何在工作中使用人工智能。研究提炼出五大洞见，并将成功的人工智能增强型开发人员的技能和知识分为四个领域：有效使用生成式人工智能、核心软件工程、相关工程以及相关非工程技能。为了应对人工智能时代的挑战，职业培训和计算机科学学位课程需要注重培养这些技术和软技能，以防止技能退化和促进职业发展。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：专业软件开发人员在人工智能时代所需技能的演变

不同观点：
• 观点一：人工智能工具的引入要求开发人员具备新的技能组合。研究通过21位开发人员的调查，明确了12个关键工作目标和75个相关任务，包括代码生成和问题理解等。这表明，开发人员不仅需要传统的软件工程技能，还需要掌握如何有效使用生成式AI工具。

• 观点二：开发人员在AI增强开发中的成功依赖于四大领域的熟练程度。这四大领域包括：有效使用生成式AI、核心软件工程技能、相邻工程学科知识以及沟通和批判性思维等非工程领域的能力。这种观点强调了跨学科能力的重要性，认为单一技能不足以应对AI时代的挑战。

• 观点三：教育和培训需要改革以适应AI集成的工作流程。该观点主张教育项目和在职培训应同时注重技术技能和软技能，以全面培养开发人员应对AI驱动的工作环境。这表明当前的教育体系可能尚未完全准备好应对这一变化。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：虽然各方都认同AI对软件开发的影响深远，但对于教育体系和培训项目如何快速适应这一变化存在争议。有人可能认为现有体系可以通过小幅调整来满足需求，而另一些人则主张需要彻底改革以确保开发人员具备全面的技能组合。

• 重要论据：研究结果提炼出的五个关键见解为如何培养下一代开发人员提供了方向，强调了多领域能力的重要性。这些任务和领域的划分提供了具体的培养路径，有助于相关方制定具体的教育和培训计划。

通过这些观点，评论明确了软件开发人员在AI时代所需的多维度技能，并指出了教育和培训体系改革的必要性。

Authors:

View a PDF of the paper titled What do professional software developers need to know to succeed in an age of Artificial Intelligence?, by Matthew Kam and 9 other authors
View PDF
Abstract:
Generative AI is showing early evidence of productivity gains for software developers, but concerns persist regarding workforce disruption and deskilling. We describe our research with 21 developers at the cutting edge of using AI, summarizing 12 of their work goals we uncovered, together with 75 associated tasks and the skills & knowledge for each, illustrating how developers use AI at work. From all of these, we distilled our findings in the form of 5 insights. We found that the skills & knowledge to be a successful AI-enhanced developer are organized into four domains (using Generative AI effectively, core software engineering, adjacent engineering, and adjacent non-engineering) deployed at critical junctures throughout a 6-step task workflow. In order to "future proof" developers for this age of AI, on-the-job learning initiatives and computer science degree programs will need to target both "soft" skills and the technical skills & knowledge in all four domains to reskill, upskill and safeguard against deskilling.
Comments:
12 pages, 4 figures, software engineering education track of the 2025 ACM international conference on the foundations of software engineering, includes supplementary material i.e. full 50-page occupational profile of the AI-enhanced software developer

data.title: Create videos with your words for free – Introducing Bing Video Creator
data.author: miles
data.article_summary: Bing推出了全新的Bing Video Creator，允许用户免费将文字描述转化为短视频。该工具由Sora技术驱动，用户只需在Bing移动应用中打开Video Creator，输入视频描述即可生成5秒长的视频，并可选择9:16格式（16:9格式即将推出）。用户一次可排队生成三个视频，完成后会收到通知，并可下载或分享视频。生成的视频免费保存90天。Bing Video Creator现已全球推出（中国和俄罗斯除外），提供快速和标准两种生成速度，前10次快速生成免费，之后可通过兑换Microsoft Rewards点数继续使用快速模式。该工具适用于纪念特别时刻、简化沟通和激发创意等多种用途，提示越详细，生成的视频效果越好。

44178536.article_content:
Questions deserve answers, ideas beg for realization, and curiosity seeks satisfaction. Two years ago, we brought this belief forward with Bing Image Creator, helping users everywhere create whatever they can imagine through words—for free. Last month, we continued the next evolution of search with
Copilot Search in Bing
, blending the best of traditional and generative search to meet you where you are at in your discovery journey.
Today we're taking the next leap with Bing Video Creator, allowing you to turn your ideas into videos, for free.
Powered by Sora, Bing Video Creator transforms your text prompts into short videos. Just describe what you want to see and watch your vision come to life.
Bing, as your AI-powered search and answer engine, not only helps you find what you need, but gives you the freedom to create exactly what you’re looking for.
Bing Video Creator is free and is rolling out starting today on the Bing Mobile App and coming soon to desktop and within Copilot Search. To get started,
download the Bing Mobile app
.
Bringing creation to your fingertips
Bing Video Creator represents our efforts to democratize the power of AI video generation. We believe creativity should be effortless and accessible to help you satisfy your answer-seeking process.
Whether you’re letting your imagination run wild, bringing a story to life, or looking for that perfect video to communicate what you’re thinking, Bing Video Creator puts the power of video creation at your fingertips. We’re excited to empower anyone to turn their words into wonder through an AI-generated video.
How to use Bing Video Creator
Getting started with Bing Video Creator is easy. Open Video Creator within the Bing Mobile app by clicking on the menu in the bottom right corner and selecting “Video Creator.” You can also type directly into the Bing mobile app search bar "Create a video of..." for quick access to video creation. Once Bing Video Creator becomes available on desktop, you can visit
Bing.com/create
.
Open the Bing app and click on the menu in the bottom right corner, then select "Video Creator."
Then, simply type in a description of the video you want to create in the prompt box. The best prompts provide additional context, description, and detail. Click “Create” and let AI generate your video. Feel free to continue dreaming up new videos – you’ll receive a notification when your video is ready to view.
Check out this fun prompt below: “In a busy Italian pizza restaurant, a small otter works as a chef and wears a chef’s hat and an apron. He kneads the dough with his paws and is surrounded by other pizza ingredients."
Videos are 5 seconds long and can be created in 9:16 format with 16:9 format coming soon. You can also queue up to three video generations at a time. If all three slots are in use, you’ll need to wait for one to finish before starting another.
Once your video is done generating, you'll receive a convenient notification informing you your video is ready. You can choose to download the video, share it via email or via your favorite social media platforms, or copy and a share a direct link to the video.
Your creations are stored for up to 90 days, giving you plenty of time to download, share, or refine your prompts.
Video creation is free to all users, with the ability to choose between Fast and Standard generation speeds. Start with 10 Fast creations to let your imagination come to life in seconds. After that, keep the creative juices flowing uninterrupted by redeeming 100
Microsoft Rewards
points for each Fast creation or continue with Standard creation speeds.*
Bing Video Creator is rolling out starting today Worldwide (Excluding China and Russia).
Use cases and inspiration
Bing Video Creator is for anyone with a story to tell. Here are some ways you can use it:
1. Special moments:
Need a quick, compelling visual to commemorate a special moment? Generate a short video that brings it to life!
2. Communication:
Turn your idea into something easy to understand, a joke into a lasting memory, or add a customized experience to your everyday conversations. Or stand out in the scroll by sharing your creation to social media.
3. Discover:
Brainstorming is now easier than ever with the ability to test creative directions, explore different styles, bring to life objects, build mood boards, and more. It's a great way to let your curiosity roam free and discover what you can imagine.
Tips and tricks
Whether you're just starting out or looking to refine your AI-generated videos, these tips will help you unlock the full potential of Bing Video Creator.
1. Be Descriptive with Your Prompts
The more vivid and specific your prompt, the better the results. Instead of “a person walking,” try “a young woman in a red coat walking through a snowy forest at sunrise.” The more detail, the better. Including camera angles and lighting also helps the model deliver what you are looking for.
2. Use Action-Oriented and Scene-setting Language

data.title: AI makes the humanities more important, but also weirder
data.author: findhorn
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI对教育和人文领域的影响以及教育系统的深层次问题

不同观点：
• gdubs认为，教育系统几十年来培养学生将学业和工作视为达成一系列无止境目标的手段，而最终目标是“找到工作”。然而，随着AI的普及，学生通过AI完成作业而非亲自阅读和培养毅力，这反映了教育和职业系统的深层次问题，而不仅仅是AI带来的新问题。
• simonw指出，有教师已经开始将课程设计转向更具挑战性的AI互动任务，如设计“ChatGPT无法完成的作业”，并认为这是一种智力挑战。
• Animats强调，传统历史教学过于注重经典和胜利者，而忽视了对失败者的研究。LLM在检测谄媚和复杂历史分析方面还不够好。
• wisty认为，评估学生的思想质量不应仅依赖于写得好的作文，教育的重点应在于教学科本身而非写作技巧。
• LurkandComment指出，在人文领域的高级学术评估中，口头答辩和现场应对能力是AI无法轻易替代的，且有些语言问题AI尚无法解决。
• dr_dshiv提到，人文领域仍有大量未被发现和翻译的文本，学生可以通过AI做出有意义的贡献，而不仅仅是完成练习任务。
• quanto认为，AI的普及将使基础编程技能商品化，从而使具备互补技能的人受益最大，特别是人文领域的人。
• neilv以讽刺的方式指出，某些系统提示可能会导致灾难性的后果，特别是在AI系统中。
• carbonguy认为，LLM对教育结构造成了巨大冲击，教育需要重新思考如何评估学习进展。
• rwmj对计算机在教育中的使用持怀疑态度，认为纸质学习更有效。
• xwowsersx认为，AI在推理和专业领域深度方面仍有局限，传统学术研究仍有其不可替代的价值。
• Tycho认为，AI可以让文学学生更轻松地获取和处理信息，从而成为顶尖的贡献者。
• mathgradthrow提到，反向图灵测试（判断是否在与AI对话）可以用于评估某些职业的适任性。
• gitfan86指出，AI可以为那些原本没有机会展示才华的人提供机会。
• throwaway75讨论了使用AI作为强大搜索引擎的伦理问题，认为AI可以帮助学生找到支持其论点的文本段落，但可能减少对文本的深入阅读。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于AI在教育中的角色及其对学生学习和评估的影响。一部分人认为AI带来了新的挑战和机会，另一部分人则担忧AI可能削弱学生对学科本身的深入理解和探索能力。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是，传统人文教育的价值以及如何在AI时代重新设计教育评估体系。
• 还有对AI技术局限性的讨论，特别是在复杂历史分析和语言理解方面的能力不足。

• simonw指出，有教师已经开始将课程设计转向更具挑战性的AI互动任务，如设计“ChatGPT无法完成的作业”，并认为这是一种智力挑战。
• Animats强调，传统历史教学过于注重经典和胜利者，而忽视了对失败者的研究。LLM在检测谄媚和复杂历史分析方面还不够好。
• wisty认为，评估学生的思想质量不应仅依赖于写得好的作文，教育的重点应在于教学科本身而非写作技巧。
• LurkandComment指出，在人文领域的高级学术评估中，口头答辩和现场应对能力是AI无法轻易替代的，且有些语言问题AI尚无法解决。
• dr_dshiv提到，人文领域仍有大量未被发现和翻译的文本，学生可以通过AI做出有意义的贡献，而不仅仅是完成练习任务。
• quanto认为，AI的普及将使基础编程技能商品化，从而使具备互补技能的人受益最大，特别是人文领域的人。
• neilv以讽刺的方式指出，某些系统提示可能会导致灾难性的后果，特别是在AI系统中。
• carbonguy认为，LLM对教育结构造成了巨大冲击，教育需要重新思考如何评估学习进展。
• rwmj对计算机在教育中的使用持怀疑态度，认为纸质学习更有效。
• xwowsersx认为，AI在推理和专业领域深度方面仍有局限，传统学术研究仍有其不可替代的价值。
• Tycho认为，AI可以让文学学生更轻松地获取和处理信息，从而成为顶尖的贡献者。
• mathgradthrow提到，反向图灵测试（判断是否在与AI对话）可以用于评估某些职业的适任性。
• gitfan86指出，AI可以为那些原本没有机会展示才华的人提供机会。
• throwaway75讨论了使用AI作为强大搜索引擎的伦理问题，认为AI可以帮助学生找到支持其论点的文本段落，但可能减少对文本的深入阅读。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于AI在教育中的角色及其对学生学习和评估的影响。一部分人认为AI带来了新的挑战和机会，另一部分人则担忧AI可能削弱学生对学科本身的深入理解和探索能力。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是，传统人文教育的价值以及如何在AI时代重新设计教育评估体系。
• 还有对AI技术局限性的讨论，特别是在复杂历史分析和语言理解方面的能力不足。

data.title: The rise of judgement over technical skill
data.author: kohlhofer
data.article_summary: 本文总结了音乐人Brian Eno在1995年对计算机音序器的观察，并将其与当今的AI工具进行类比。Eno认为，音序器让技术技能不再成为障碍，取而代之的是判断力。如今，AI工具正在使写作、图像生成、编码和数据分析等领域的大量创意和专业任务变得大众化。关键区别不在于能否完成任务，而在于判断力：知道该做什么、做出有意义的选择、评估质量以及理解背景。随着AI发展，未来工作将更注重战略判断，能够提出正确问题、有效界定问题、做出明智决策并为AI工具提供有意义指导的人将最具价值。Eno的观察为AI时代提供了蓝图，强调判断力是最宝贵的资产。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：

• **tingle** 引用达芬奇的名言，强调判断力超越作品本身是一个好的迹象，表明画家有潜力达到完美，隐喻在AI辅助下，人类判断力的重要性。
• **physicsguy** 提到，批判性分析能力固然重要，但需要建立在一定的知识基础之上。同时，批评公司技术栈统一决策不当，指出这并未解决实际开发者面临的问题。
• **nluken** 批评科技行业用“民主化”来掩盖降低技术门槛的商业动机，认为LLMs（大型语言模型）本质上是中立的，但被用于财富和权力争夺。
• **mehulashah** 认为，领导者的判断力使他们能够扩大影响力，即使他们的具体技能可能已不如从前。
• **TrackerFF** 指出，AI在提供起点和大局观方面很有帮助，但在处理 obscure 问题时，生成的代码可能过时或不支持。
• **scj** 用建筑蓝图的比喻说明，AI可以设计美观的外表，但缺乏支撑结构的深度，技术知识仍是判断的基础。
• **lordnacho** 表示，技术技能和判断力相辅相成，AI只是改变了边界，未来需要更高层次的判断力来处理复杂的产品。
• **CleverLikeAnOx** 批评文章结论冗余，认为如果没有AI辅助，作者可能不会写出这样的内容。
• **0x445442** 强调，良好的判断力需要对基础有深入的理解，就像音乐作曲家需要精通乐器一样。
• **red_admiral** 认为，系统设计和边界划分等需要经验的人类判断，AI尚无法胜任。
• **overfl0w** 引用阿西莫夫的《Jokester》故事，探讨提出正确问题的重要性，AI需要人类提供有意义的提问。
• **wg0** 强调，判断力依赖于技能，主张亲身学习并掌握技术。
• **layer8** 指出，当判断告诉你是错的，你需要技术技能来知道什么是对的，并质疑AI何时能超越人类的判断力和技术技能。
• **dwoldrich** 认为，AI可以提升工作质量，但依赖于输入的质量，并担心AI过于强大可能导致人类停止学习。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于AI能否替代人类的判断力和技术技能，尤其是在复杂和创造性任务中的角色。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是AI在不同领域的“民主化”影响，以及这种影响是否被合理化或过度美化。
• 经验与基础知识在AI辅助时代的重要性被多次强调，表明即使在AI时代，人类专长仍不可替代。

44153732.article_content:
A version of this post was first published on
MapsAll
.
In 1995, musician and producer Brian Eno made a profound observation about computer sequencers that has become increasingly relevant in our AI-powered world:
“The great benefit of computer sequencers is that they remove the issue of skill, and replace it with the issue of judgement. With Cubase or Photoshop, anybody can actually do anything, and you can make stuff that sounds very much like stuff you’d hear on the radio, or looks very much like anything you see in magazines. So the question becomes not whether you can do it or not, because any drudge can do it if they’re prepared to sit in front of the computer for a few days, the question then is, ‘Of all the things you can now do, which do you choose to do?’”
The Parallel to AI
Eno’s insight perfectly captures what’s happening with AI tools today. Just as computer sequencers democratized music production, AI is democratizing a wide range of creative and professional tasks:
Writing and content creation
Image generation and design
Code development
Data analysis
Problem-solving
The technical barriers that once separated amateurs from professionals are rapidly dissolving. Anyone with access to AI tools can now produce work that, at least superficially, resembles professional output.
The New Differentiator: Judgement
As Eno predicted, the key differentiator is no longer technical skill but judgement. When everyone can generate content, code, or designs, the real value lies in:
Knowing what to create
: Understanding what’s worth making in the first place
Making meaningful choices
: Selecting the right approach from countless possibilities
Evaluating quality
: Distinguishing between good and great outputs
Understanding context
: Applying the right solution to the right problem
The Future of Work
As AI continues to evolve, we’ll see more roles shift from technical execution to strategic judgement. The most valuable professionals will be those who can:
Ask the right questions
Frame problems effectively
Make sound decisions
Provide meaningful direction to AI tools
Conclusion
Eno’s observation from nearly 30 years ago has become a blueprint for thriving in the AI era. The question is no longer “Can you do it?” but “What should you do, and why?” As technical barriers continue to fall, our ability to exercise good judgement becomes our most valuable asset.

data.title: Twain Dreams
data.author: samclemens
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了塞缪尔·克莱门斯（即马克·吐温）在2025年，即哈珀杂志175周年之际可能出现的复兴。文章提到作家Percival Everett在2024年的小说《James》重新诠释了吐温的《哈克贝利·费恩历险记》中自解放的黑奴Jim的视角，并获得了国家图书奖。此外，斯坦福教授Shelley Fisher Fishkin也出版了关于Jim的新书。同时，今年的马克·吐温美国幽默奖由喜剧演员Conan O'Brien获得，他在获奖演讲中借吐温反对霸凌和种族主义，含蓄批评了当前政权。文章还提到Ron Chernow的新吐温传记出版，显示吐温在文化记忆中的持久影响力。作者反思吐温的持久“相关性”，并提到喜剧演员Dave Chappelle在2019年获奖时对吐温的隐晦引用。文章最后讲述了作者自己与吐温的个人联系。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对马克·吐温和其作品《哈克贝利·费恩历险记》的解读及其个人历史中的争议

不同观点：
• Daisywh：首次阅读《哈克芬》时并未深刻理解，多年后重读，意识到吐温作品中的尖锐性，尤其是隐藏的愤怒。她认为吐温的作品不断引发新的思考和讨论，且推测吐温会对互联网时代的各种现象有独特见解。
• sp1nningaway：对文章的句法感到困惑，认为简单的句式更易理解，对复杂的句法表示不适。
• Zorass：同意吐温作品中展现的内在矛盾使其作品具有永恒的魅力，能够触动现代读者。他赞赏吐温的真实和细腻的描绘，将其视为珍贵的存在。
• the_af：质疑文章中关于吐温早期是种族主义者的断言，认为缺乏证据支持。他引用吐温在南北战争中的短暂经历，指出吐温很快退出军队，且吐温本人对战争的政治背景感到困惑，不应简单将其归类为种族主义者。
• mock-possum：对文章表示赞赏，认为值得花时间阅读。他提到重读《哈克芬》可能会带来新的理解，尤其是与经典文学主题的关联。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于吐温是否曾是种族主义者。the_af对此提出质疑，认为文章中的断言缺乏充分证据，并引用外部来源支持自己的观点。
• 讨论中还涉及到吐温作品的永恒性和多重解读性，Daisywh和Zorass都提到吐温作品能够不断引发新的思考，并反映出吐温个人的复杂性。
• 句法和文章的可读性也是讨论的一个方面，sp1nningaway认为复杂的句法影响了阅读体验，显示出对文章风格的不同偏好。

44161102.article_content:
June 2025 Issue
[Symposium]
Twain Dreams
Adjust
Share
The enigma of Samuel Clemens
by
John Jeremiah Sullivan
,
Mark Twain on the steps leading up to his study at Quarry Farm, New York, 1903, by T. E. Marr. Courtesy the Center for Mark Twain Studies, Elmira College, New York
Could some kind of Mark Twain revival be afoot in this, the 175th-anniversary year of
Harperâs Magazine,
a periodical that more consistently than any other provided a home for Twainâs writing during the half-century-long major phase of his career?Â
1
The signs are come unto us. The writer Percival Everettâs 2024 novel
James,
in which Everett reimagines the story of Twainâs
Adventures of Huckleberry Finn
from the perspective of Huckâs raft mate on the Mississippi, the self-emancipated Jim, took home last yearâs National Book Award for Fiction. Only two months ago, we got a major new book by the Stanford professor Shelley Fisher Fishkin, who in the long history of scholarship on Mark Twain has written some of the best of it.
Jim
is the title, and subject, of Fishkinâs latest. So, we have
James
and
Jim,
barely a year apart. Meanwhile, the annual Mark Twain Prize for American Humor has taken on new significance as a sort of dissenterâs pulpit. This yearâs winner, the comedian and talk-show host Conan OâBrien, seized the moment of his acceptance speech, delivered in March onstage at the Kennedy Center in Washingtonâwhere the previous month, the board of trustees had been ousted by President Trump and replaced with a shock brigade of his sort of people, among them the country singer Lee Greenwood, of âProud to Be an Americanâ fame, all in the interest of ushering in a new âGolden Age in Arts and Culture,â with Trump himself at the head, as chair, lobbing brain-damaged non sequiturs about this one time he saw
Cats
âand used it, OâBrien did, to speak out not-so-subtly against the regime. âTwain hated bullies,â OâBrien told the crowd, a statement largely true (although Tom Sawyer was a bully at times, and a manipulative narcissist at all times). OâBrien said that Twain hated racism too, and it is true that Twain
came
to hate racism, although he had been a racist earlier in his life and even farcically fought for the Confederacy for a couple of weeks. But this is pedantry on my part.
2
Most recently, a major new Twain biography has been published, by Ron Chernow, one of our great Biographers of the Great (on some future day he, Walter Isaacson, and Jon Meacham will write biographies of one another, and the faces on Mount Rushmore will simultaneously explode). The mere fact that Chernow has chosen Twain to stand in as the sole
littÃ©rateur
on his list of targeted cities, a lineup that otherwise comprises none but political or financial world-shakers, e.g., Washington, Hamilton, Grant, Morgan, and Rockefellerâsays something about Twainâs place in our collective cultural memory, his âongoing relevance,â maybe, although, in this case, not exactly:
relevance
would imply that he continues to play a loosely agreed-upon role in our self-understanding, or that his life and work imply some standard we fear to disappoint, whereas with Twain it seems more the case that we go on
suspecting he hides some meaning,
some message that we could probably use, behind the bushy eyebrows and mustache, but are less and less able to name or remember. He doesnât quite haunt us. OâBrien had to perform some impressive textual excavation to make Twain serve the nightâs theme. The author âpopulated his works with abusers such as Huck Finnâs alcoholic father and Tom Driscoll in
Puddânhead Wilson,
â the comedian said, âand he made his readers passionately hate those characters.â Ah, yes, Tom Driscoll, born 1/32 black, swapped out in infancy by his mother and raised as a lazy white Southern aristocratÂ . . . or possibly the other, ârealâ Tom Driscoll, born white but raised enslaved? . . . Either way, God damn them
and
Pap Finn! The comedian Dave Chappelle, who won the 2019 Mark Twain Prize, may have shown wisdom in keeping his own Twain references more oblique. He said nothing, in fact, about Twain. At one point he reportedly put his face down beside the bronze trophy bust of Twain that the organizers placed onstage for the ceremony, and grinned enigmatically. What did that mean? Something about Twain and race and America and now? Could he feel Everettâs novel coming, know that the script was about to be flipped?
I grew up so hopelessly steeped in the cult of Twain that I have to perform a mental adjustment to understand how a Twain revival could be possible. How does one revive what is ever-present and oppressively urgent? 44161102.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了塞缪尔·克莱门斯（即马克·吐温）在2025年，即哈珀杂志175周年之际可能出现的复兴。文章提到作家Percival Everett在2024年的小说《James》重新诠释了吐温的《哈克贝利·费恩历险记》中自解放的黑奴Jim的视角，并获得了国家图书奖。此外，斯坦福教授Shelley Fisher Fishkin也出版了关于Jim的新书。同时，今年的马克·吐温美国幽默奖由喜剧演员Conan O'Brien获得，他在获奖演讲中借吐温反对霸凌和种族主义，含蓄批评了当前政权。文章还提到Ron Chernow的新吐温传记出版，显示吐温在文化记忆中的持久影响力。作者反思吐温的持久“相关性”，并提到喜剧演员Dave Chappelle在2019年获奖时对吐温的隐晦引用。文章最后讲述了作者自己与吐温的个人联系。

data.title: Against "Against Life Extension"
data.author: quadrin
data.article_summary:
Alex Kesin的这篇文章回应了Francis Fukuyama对寿命延长研究的反对意见。Kesin认为，寿命延长在伦理上必要且经济上合理，反对它等同于忽视医学成就。Fukuyama的观点基于两点：生理上的不可能和社会政治僵化，但这些论点都站不住脚。

在生物学方面，Kesin反驳了“打地鼠”式的质疑，指出通过针对个别疾病的干预已显著改善健康寿命，且这些干预具有协同效应。社会文化方面，Kesin认为认知僵化并非长寿必然结果，历史上有许多人在晚年仍能创新。此外，长寿并不必然导致社会停滞，反而可能带来更多创新和智慧积累。

总之，Fukuyama的逻辑错误地将死亡与社会变革必要性挂钩，而真正的挑战在于如何在延长健康寿命的同时保持社会适应性。

不同观点：
• [absurdo] 认为原作者的反驳是无效的，因为原文只是个人观点的宣泄，而非科学或哲学论述。absurdo 进一步指出，反对富人通过支付来延长寿命至200岁并没有太大的争议，并认为世界已经处于灾难之中，由“虐待狂”控制，因此延长寿命的讨论并没有实际意义。

• [slibhb] 支持寿命延长研究，但指出一个根本反对意见：死亡创造变化，因此死亡是必要的。slibhb 认为，人类成年后可能难以改变，因此大幅延长寿命可能导致文明停滞，并认为这一论点不易克服。

争议焦点：
• 延长寿命的伦理问题：是否会导致文明停滞和社会不平等的加剧。
• 对 Fukuyama 逻辑的批评和辩护，特别是关于“死亡是必要的”这一前提是否成立。
• 寿命延长研究的动机和受益者，特别是对社会资源分配公平性的影响。
